en: What Is an Empire?
zh: 何为帝国？

en: Byzantium is conventionally called an empire, but it is not at first sight evident that this term withstands critical scrutiny. Beyond mere convention and inertia, there is no systematic investigation of whether or to what degree Romanía fits definitions of empire that are used by scholars who specialize in the history of empires. This field has surged in the past two decades or so, especially after the belated admission that the United States is also an empire of sorts, which has prompted a great deal of comparative work. How “imperial” might Romanía appear if it is brought out of the insular shell of Byzantine Studies and required to play by the rules that have evolved for the comparative study of empires? This will be the first attempt of its kind. I must therefore quote John Haldon, who, in a similar context, wrote that “it is only with some difficulty that I can present a critique of the preexisting literature on the comparative situation and evolution of the Byzantine state, since there is so little to discuss.”
There is a total lack of theoretical reflection and empirical inquiry on the issue of whether Romanía was an empire.
zh: 拜占庭约定俗成地被称为一个帝国，但乍看之下，这个词能否经得起批判性审视并不明显。除了单纯的惯例与惰性之外，并没有系统的研究去考察罗曼尼亚是否符合、或在多大程度上符合那些专治帝国史的学者所使用的帝国定义。这一领域在过去二十年左右迅猛发展，尤其是在人们迟迟才承认美国也是某种意义上的帝国之后，这催生了大量比较研究。如果把罗曼尼亚从相对封闭的拜占庭研究中带出来，放到帝国比较研究的框架下考察，它在多大程度上称得上帝国？这将是此类尝试中的第一次。因此我必须引用约翰·哈尔顿，他在类似语境中写道：“我只有费一番力气，才能对现有文献就拜占庭国家在比较视野下的处境与演变作一评议，因为可讨论的东西实在太少。”
关于罗曼尼亚是否是一个帝国这个问题，理论反思与实证探究都完全阙如。

en: There are three reasons we might call Romanía an empire, only one of which is a good one. The other two reasons are that it was a direct continuation of the ancient

and that its monarch may in some fashion have called himself an emperor (regardless of whether what he ruled was an empire). Let us set these reasons aside for a moment and stick with the more general and cross-disciplinary definition. After all, if we want Romanía to participate in broader discussions about empire, it needs to follow common rules. Limiting the discussion to heirs of the old
would leave a set of exactly one (or two, if we allow the Germans to crash the party), which is a recipe for isolation.
zh: 我们称罗曼尼亚为帝国，可能有三个理由，其中只有一个站得住脚。另外两个理由是：它是古代
（罗马国家）的直接延续，以及其君主可能以某种方式自称皇帝（无论他所统治的是否是一个帝国）。让我们暂且把这些理由搁置一旁，按更普遍、不同学科共同适用的定义来考察。毕竟，要把罗曼尼亚纳入关于帝国的更广泛讨论，就得按通用的尺度考察它。把讨论限定于古老
的继承者，将只剩下恰好一个（或两个，如果我们允许德意志人来凑热闹）成员，这无异于自我孤立。

en: What is an empire? I distil here from recent bibliography what seems to be a conventional current understanding.

An empire is a state that results from the conquest or subjugation by one state or ethnic group of a number of other states or peoples. The conquering state does not have to be a monarchy that is ruled by an “emperor”: for instance, democratic Athens and Republican Rome have been studied as empires. Empires do not emerge from the mere titles of monarchs or the political arrangements internal to the conquerors. They are instead defined by an awareness, maintenance, and enforcement of ethnic, cultural, political, or religious differences between the conquerors and conquered. Empire places the two in a hierarchical relationship defined by legal distinctions and differential rights and responsibilities that often entail exploitation based on precisely those differences. The contrast is typically accentuated by the geographical separation of the metropolis or core territory, where the majority of the ruling group or nation lives, from the subjugated peoples who populate the provinces. Therefore, empires are almost by definition multiethnic. “The key marker of an ‘imperial’ state was thus the degree of ‘foreign-ness’ perceived to exist between rulers and ruled, conquerors and conquered.”
And, “empire is differentiated: religiously, nationally, occupationally, and territorially. . . . [It] usually subordinates diverse ethnolinguistic groups or would-be nations.”

Empires are often large, but it is neither necessary nor possible to specify an absolute requirement of size. The perception that empires are big stems from the fact that they subsume several states or peoples and thus expand the scale of the conquering polity.
zh: 何为帝国？我在此从近期文献中提炼出一种似乎是当前通行的理解。

帝国是这样一种国家：它由一个国家或族群征服或控制若干其他国家或民族而形成。征服国不必是由一位“皇帝”统治的君主国：例如，民主雅典与共和罗马都曾被作为帝国来研究。帝国并非产生于君主的单纯头衔或征服者内部的政治安排。帝国的特征在于，统治者意识到征服者与被征服者之间存在族群、文化、政治或宗教差别，并设法维持、强制推行这些差别。帝国把两者置于一种等级关系之中，这种关系由法律上的区分以及不同的权利与义务所界定，剥削也往往就建立在这些差别之上。这种对照通常因地理上的分隔而加剧：统治群体或民族的大多数所居住的中心地区或核心领土，和各行省受其统治的族群处于不同地域。因此，帝国几乎从定义上就是多族群的。“因此，一个‘帝国’国家的关键标志，是统治者和被统治者、征服者和被征服者之间感受到的‘外族差异’有多大。”
还有，“帝国是有分化的：在宗教上、民族上、职业上和领土上。……［它］通常使各种族群语言共同体或潜在民族处于从属地位。”
帝国往往庞大，但既无必要也不可能规定一个绝对的规模要求。认为帝国庞大的看法源于这样一个事实：它们把若干国家或民族纳入自身，从而扩大了征服性政治共同体的规模。

en: Empires are enormously varied within the broad parameters set by this definition, for example in the ways that they exercise control over their provinces (direct vs. indirect, or formal vs. informal). Empires are typically segmented: the various conquered regions are usually not in contact with each other but only with the imperial center, resulting in a hub-and-spoke structure.
In the Roman and Byzantine cases, the rim holding the spokes together was the armies along the frontier periphery. A popular recent distinction is that between states that

In the latter case, the loss of empire cannot easily be imagined without a fundamental reconceptualization of the “core” polity, assuming that it can easily be identified (the Sasanian Persian, Arab, and Ottoman empires come to mind here). en: If we apply the above definitions to earlier phases of Roman history, we obtain some counterintuitive results. Specifically, what we call “the Republic” was far more imperialistic than “the empire.” The latter in fact gradually wound down the history of Roman conquests. Also, Rome had an empire long before it had an emperor.
But we begin to call it an empire only when it acquires an emperor. The modern taxonomy of ancient Roman history tracks changes in the domestic politics of the

that are extraneous to the definition of empire that is used by comparative historians today. This is because domestic politics were (and still are) more important in the tradition of western political thought than international relations. Whereas the rest of this chapter will examine Romanía in light of the general definition of empire presented above, we must consider the two other reasons for calling it an empire that I mentioned above, namely that it was the continuation of the ancient

and that its ruler may have claimed to be an “emperor.” These are not good reasons for calling Romanía an empire in a theoretical or comparative context, but they explain why it has conventionally been called that.
zh: 如果把上述定义应用于罗马历史的较早阶段，我们会得到一些反直觉的结果。具体而言，我们所谓的“共和国”远比“帝国”更具帝国主义色彩。后者事实上逐渐结束了罗马以征服来扩张的历史。而且，罗马早在拥有皇帝之前很久就已拥有了一个帝国。
但我们只是在它获得一位皇帝时才开始称它为帝国。现代对古罗马历史的分期，追踪的是
（罗马国家）的内部政治的变化，而这些变化与今天比较史家所使用的帝国定义无关。这是因为在西方政治思想传统中，对内政治过去（且现在仍然）比国际关系更重要。尽管本章其余部分将依据上文提出的帝国一般定义来审视罗曼尼亚，我们还必须考虑我上文提到的另外两个称它为帝国的理由，即它是古代

en: The Latin term

from which we get the word “empire,” did not originally mean that; in fact, it is likely that it never meant that in antiquity. Its original meaning was the power or authority vested in a Roman magistrate. In the late Republic, it could refer to the power of the Roman people as a whole. It was only later, and by extension from this original sense, that it came to acquire a territorial sense, as referring to the lands and people subject to Rome. But even in this sense it did not primarily point to the relation of domination that obtained between Romans and non-Romans. “Subjugation” was not its original meaning and even the emperors used the term

to refer primarily to the power of their position within the “domestic” Roman political system, not to the rule of Romans over non-Romans. On the other hand, generals who were victorious in battle were acclaimed as
as having conquered their enemy, who was usually a foreign foe. Some received triumphs for this but these were “granted for military success, not for empire-building.”
So

could point to what we have defined as empire, but it was not a technical word for it. Moreover, the main “titles” of the Roman emperors were Caesar and Augustus, which did not point to any kind of “imperial” position at all.

en: These terms, or a nominalist approach in general, are not going to make Romanía into an empire for us. Moreover, the fact that Romanía was a direct continuation of the ancient Roman
also does not prove that it was an empire proper, because the ancient
underwent fundamental changes that call its continued status as an empire into doubt. In 212, all free people of the

were made into Roman citizens; provincials from formerly conquered peoples increasingly began to fill the highest offices in the state, including the imperial office; there was considerable assimilation of the provincials to the evolving consensus Roman norms; and the emperors and their courts left Rome to reside primarily in the provinces. In these ways, the empire transformed itself from a state in which Romans ruled over non-Romans into a large, unified, and increasingly homogeneous state in which the same rights were distributed across the territory, fractally reproducing Roman social structures regardless of prior ethnicity. Power was no longer exercised by Romans upon non-Romans, whom they had previously called their “slaves.” The ruling class, armies, and the emperors themselves were provincialized, while the provinces were Romanized.
Exploitation and inequality were no longer a function of territory, the history of subject peoples, or ethnicity.
zh: 这些词语，或一般而言的唯名论进路，并不会替我们把罗曼尼亚变成一个帝国。此外，罗曼尼亚是古代罗马
的直接延续这一事实，也不能证明它是一个严格意义上的帝国，因为古代
经历了根本性变化，使人怀疑它作为帝国的延续地位。212年，

内所有自由人都成为罗马公民；来自先前被征服民族的行省居民，日益开始充任国家最高官职，包括皇位；行省居民大量同化于不断演变、逐渐为众人接受的罗马规范；皇帝及其宫廷离开罗马，主要驻跸于行省。通过这些方式，帝国把自己从一个罗马人统治非罗马人的国家，转变为一个庞大、统一、日益同质的国家，无论先前的族群如何，各地居民一体享有相同的权利，各级地方社会也不断形成与罗马相似的结构。权力不再由罗马人施加于非罗马人——他们此前曾称后者为自己的“奴隶”。统治阶级、军队乃至皇帝本身都被行省化了，而行省则被罗马化了。
剥削与不平等不再取决于地域、被征服者的历史或族群身份。

en: In many publications, Cliff Ando has argued that, if “empires function through the cultivation of difference” such that “those belonging to the center are equal among themselves in contradistinction to those over whom they [exercise] a collective rule,” then Rome after the third century “constitutes a special case.”
The universal grant of citizenship was “no less than an unprecedented act of imperial self-abrogation,” which turned Rome into a different kind of polity.
“One might even say that it ceased in any meaningful way to be an empire. It became, rather, something like a state . . . a state that
rather than a state that
an empire—with a uniform law of persons and legal culture, both penetrating universally throughout its territory.”
Linking Romanía to the tail end of this development will not, therefore, establish it as an empire; quite the contrary.

普遍授予公民权“无异于一次史无前例的帝国自我废除之举”，它把罗马变成了另一种政治共同体。
“人们甚至可以说，它在任何有意义的层面上都不再是一个帝国。它毋宁变成了某种类似国家的东西……一个
帝国而非
帝国的国家——拥有统一的人身法与法律文化，两者都普遍渗透于其整个领土。”
因此，指出罗曼尼亚承继了这一演变的结果，并不能确立它为帝国；恰恰相反。

en: The official and nonofficial titles of the rulers of Romanía do not signal that they ruled over an empire, that is, over Romans

non-Romans. Compare the Achaemenid Persian title “king of kings”; the Sasanian Persian title “king of kings of the Aryans and non-Aryans” (though it is not clear who these subordinate kings were supposed to be); the full titles of the Ottoman sultans that listed all the provinces of their empire;

and the long list of territorial and other dependencies still appended to the British and Spanish Crowns. As a Roman equivalent of such lists of conquered peoples or territories we might take the triumphal

appended to the imperial title, which named the nations that each emperor had conquered—Alamannicus, Germanicus, and so on. But these indicated only that a people had been defeated in a battle, not necessarily that they had been annexed by the empire and ruled as ethnically different subjects. Moreover, that tradition seems to have lapsed after the seventh century, though it was once revived after a long hiatus, by Manuel I Komnenos, for one occasion in 1166.
zh: 罗曼尼亚统治者的正式与非正式头衔，并不表明他们统治着一个帝国，即统治着罗马人
非罗马人。试比较阿契美尼德波斯的头衔“万王之王”；萨珊波斯的头衔“雅利安人与非雅利安人的万王之王”（尽管不清楚这些从属国王究竟指谁）；奥斯曼苏丹列举其帝国所有行省的完整头衔；
以及仍附加于不列颠与西班牙王室之上的那一长串领土及其他属地。罗马也有与这种列举被征服民族或土地的做法相近的例子，那就是附于帝号的凯旋
（尊号），它们标明每位皇帝所征服的民族——阿拉曼尼库斯（Alamannicus）、日耳曼尼库斯（Germanicus）等等。但这些只表明一个民族在一场战役中被击败，未必表明他们已被帝国吞并、并作为另一个族群的臣民接受统治。此外，那一传统似乎在七世纪之后就已废止，尽管在长期中断之后曾一度被曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁恢复，仅见于1166年的一次正式场合。

en: Formal titles will not get us to empire, nor are they necessary. After all, not all empires have monarchs with suitably “imperial” titles, nor are they all even monarchies.

Byzantinists are wedded to the idea that the Byzantine ruler called himself an emperor and his realm an empire. We take this for granted so much that we use those terms even for its final days when it included only the capital, a few islands, and the Peloponnese. This prompts many historians to comment on the gap between names and reality: “It was an ‘empire’ in name only.”
But perhaps it was not an empire even in name.
zh: 有无正式帝号，都不足以判定一个国家是否是帝国。毕竟，并非所有帝国都有头衔恰如其分地“帝国式的”君主，甚至并非所有帝国都是君主国。
拜占庭学家固执着这样一种观念：拜占庭统治者自称皇帝，其国度自称帝国。我们太习惯于把这看成理所当然的事，以至于即便到了末期只剩都城、几座岛屿和伯罗奔尼撒时，我们还用这样的称呼。这促使许多史家评论名实之间的差距：“它只是一个名义上的‘帝国’。”
但也许它甚至连名义上都不是一个帝国。

en: The core title of the Byzantine ruler was

of the Romans (“faithful in Christ”), which in plain Greek means “king of the Romans” and was probably taken by his subjects to mean just that: they were the Romans and he was their monarch. Having said that, the

of the Romans was not any king. Both he and his subjects believed that he was superior to other kings. But this does not mean that he was an “emperor” in the sense that he was an über-monarch who ruled over non-Roman realms. If that idea forms part of our intuition regarding medieval rulers, it comes from the German tradition, not the Roman one. It was the Germans who began the practice of formally promoting the “
of the Germans” to the notional status of “

of the Romans,” but this did not correspond to anything in Roman titulature or practice. The idea that an emperor is a monarch who rules over a number of subordinate kings, barons, dukes, cities, archbishops, and peoples, thus making him the lord of a loosely federated and multiethnic empire, is also a medieval German convention.
In Romanía, the
was primarily the monarch of the Roman people. If at a given time he did not rule over non-Romans, that did not make him any less a

of the Romans or any less superior in status to foreign kings. Moreover, although his position was understood to be superior to that of barbarian kings, their realms did not have to be parts of his own for that to be the case.
zh: 拜占庭统治者的核心头衔是罗马人的
（“忠于基督者”），用平实的希腊语说就是“罗马人的国王”，而他的臣民大概也正是这样理解的：他们是罗马人，他是他们的君主。话虽如此，罗马人的
地位有别于一般国王。他和他的臣民都相信他高于其他国王。但这并不意味着他是一个“皇帝”——即统治着非罗马国度的超级君主意义上的皇帝。如果那种观念是我们一想到中世纪君主就容易产生的印象，那它来自德意志传统，而非罗马传统。正是德意志人开创了这样一种做法：把“德意志人的
（国王）”正式晋为名义上的“罗马人的
（皇帝）”，但这在罗马的头衔体系或实践中并无任何对应。皇帝是一位统治着若干从属国王、男爵、公爵、城市、大主教与民族的君主，从而成为一个松散联合的多族群帝国之主——这种观念也是一种中世纪德意志惯例。
在罗曼尼亚，
首先是罗马人民的君主。如果在某个时候他并不统治非罗马人，那也丝毫不减损他作为罗马人的
的身份，或丝毫不减损他在地位上高于外国国王。此外，尽管他的地位被理解为高于蛮族国王，但那些国王的国度不必是他自己国度的一部分，这一点也依然成立。

en: Consider for example the sixth-century political theorist Ioannes Lydos. He claims that the position of Caesar is superior to that of king

because the (Roman) Caesars used to appoint kings to rule the various foreign nations. He is referring here to the tradition of Rome’s client kings, whose realms were not governed directly by imperial administrators but which were dependent in various ways. Yet this relationship is not how he
a Caesar. Two chapters earlier he had defined the Caesars in terms of their relationship to the rest of the Roman polity—τὰ κοινά, “the commons.” He slots the term
in here, as the function of commanding the Roman army.
None of this requires empire as such, an ongoing relationship of domination of non-Romans by Romans.
zh: 试以六世纪政治理论家约安尼斯·吕多斯为例。他声称凯撒的地位高于国王
，因为（罗马的）凯撒们过去常常任命国王去统治各个外族。他这里指的是罗马附庸国王的传统，那些国王的国度不由帝国行政官直接治理，但会以多种方式依附罗马。然而这种关系并非他
凯撒的方式。在两章之前，他曾依据凯撒与罗马政治共同体其余部分——τὰ κοινά，即“公共事务”——的关系来定义凯撒。在这里，
一词指的是统率罗马军队的职责。
这一切都不要求帝国本身，即罗马人对非罗马人的一种持续支配关系。

en: In his discussion of whether the Athenian empire was really an empire, Ian Morris correctly warns against approaching the question as “a philological exercise,” with the central question being how we translate terms that appear in the sources. This way “we are ducking the analytical challenge.” Fundamentally, we should “think of empires as a type of state, characterized by a strong sense of foreignness between rulers and ruled.”
So was Romanía an empire? Or did it instead only have an empire? In which case, how much of it was empire and how much not?
zh: 伊恩·莫里斯在讨论雅典帝国是否真是一个帝国时，正确地警告不要把这个当作“一道语文学题目”来处理，即以我们如何翻译史料中出现的词语为中心问题。这样做“我们是在回避分析上的挑战”。根本上，我们应当“把帝国视为一种国家类型，其特征是统治者和被统治者之间强烈的异族感”。
那么罗曼尼亚是一个帝国吗？抑或它只是拥有一个帝国？若是后者，帝国领地在罗曼尼亚占多大比重，又有多少领土不属于这种领地？

en: Empire and Difference in Romanía
zh: 罗曼尼亚的帝国统治与差异

en: To ascertain whether Romanía was an empire we must weigh the balance of difference and domination within it, and we mean a particular kind of difference. The difference between rich and poor is not an imperial relationship, but one of socioeconomic inequality that can exist between Romans. That type of rule may have been exploitative, but it does not make a state into an empire. (Also, we have no reason to think Romanía was more exploitative of its “own” people than other developed states.) “Two different logics of exclusion operated within imperial cores and peripheries—in the former those tended to be exclusions of social status, wealth, gender and citizenship, while in the peripheries exclusions operated along lines of race, ethnicity, and civilization.”
zh: 要确定罗曼尼亚是否是一个帝国，必须考察其内部有哪些群体差别、实行何种支配关系。这里所说的差异有特定含义。富人与穷人之间的差异不是一种帝国关系，而是一种可能存在于罗马人之间的社会经济不平等。那种统治可能是剥削性的，但它并不使一个国家成为帝国。（而且，我们没有理由认为罗曼尼亚比其它发达国家更剥削它“自己的”人民。）“两种不同的排斥逻辑在帝国核心与边缘内部运作——在核心，排斥通常以社会地位、财富、性别和公民身份为依据，而在边缘，排斥则依照种族、族群和文明的界线发生。”

en: The Romans of Byzantium encompassed its Greek-speaking Orthodox population, which was the majority at all times. No cultural, religious, or ethnic differences existed between the Romans of the court, capital, and army and those of the provinces, save for what we would expect: some were wealthier, some more snobbish, some had weapons, and some were farmers. But otherwise there was no ethnic or legal barrier that provincial Romans had to overcome in order to join the army of the Romans, hold office in the state or Church, or rise to the throne. They were not marked as “other” by the ruling elite. They did not, then, constitute a community governed by imperial articulations of difference. Empire must be sought in Roman rule over the non-Romans. Were there enough non-Romans in Romanía such that we can classify it as an empire? Who were they?
zh: 拜占庭的罗马人涵盖了其说希腊语的正教人口，这一人口在任何时候都是多数。宫廷、都城与军队的罗马人，同行省的罗马人之间，并不存在文化、宗教或族群差异，除了我们能预料到的那些：有些人更富有，有些人更势利，有些人有武器，有些人是农民。但除此之外，行省罗马人想要加入罗马人的军队、在国家或教会中任职、或登上皇位，并不需要克服任何族群或法律障碍。他们没有被统治精英标记为“他者”。因此，他们并不构成一个按照帝国特有的差别待遇来统治的共同体。要找帝国统治的证据，就得看罗马人如何治理非罗马人。罗曼尼亚是否有足够多的非罗马人，使我们能把它归类为一个帝国？他们是谁？

en: There is no shortage of statements in the scholarship that Byzantium was a multiethnic empire marked by extraordinary diversity in both language and ethnicity. These general statements are made by Byzantinists,
comparative scholars of empire who rely on them,
and authors of historical fiction.

The metaphor of an ethnic “mosaic” is thrown about a lot, and I suspect that some historians infer circularly that Byzantium was multiethnic simply from the fact that we call it an empire, because that is what empires are. Some versions of this view project onto Byzantium the image of a Central Asian empire, with tribes, loosely allied to the emperor, wandering its provinces; whereas others project onto it the image of Ottoman Constantinople, a cosmopolitan city of many faiths where Jews, Armenians, and Latins rubbed shoulders with Greeks and Turks, all devoted to commerce. These images are anachronistic and inaccurate, but the very premise of the multiethnic empire on which they rest is also problematic. Consider that no historian of Byzantium has done the actual work to document this alleged ethnic diversity, namely the existence, nature, and size of the “ethnic minorities” whose “very existence challenged the concept of Byzantine uniformity.”
The present chapter will be the first to do so, and it will argue that these minorities do not greatly compromise Byzantine uniformity.
zh: 学界不乏这样的论断：拜占庭是一个多族群帝国，以语言与族群两方面的非凡多样性为特征。做出这些笼统论断的，有拜占庭学家，
有依赖拜占庭学者研究的帝国比较史家，
还有历史小说作家。

族群“马赛克”的比喻常被随意使用，而我怀疑有些史家循环论证：仅仅因为我们称拜占庭为帝国，就推断它是多族群的，因为帝国本来就是那样的。这种观点的某些版本把一种中亚帝国的形象投射到拜占庭身上：与皇帝松散结盟的部落在其行省间游荡；另一些版本则把奥斯曼君士坦丁堡的形象投射到它身上：一个多种信仰并存的国际都会，犹太人、亚美尼亚人和拉丁人与希腊人、突厥人摩肩接踵，全都投身商业。这些形象既时代错置又不准确，但它们所依赖的多族群帝国这一前提本身也有问题。试想，没有一位拜占庭史家做过实际工作来记录这种所谓的族群多样性，即那些“少数族群”的存在、性质与规模——它们的“存在本身挑战了拜占庭一致性的概念”。
本章将是第一个这样做的，并将论证这些少数族群并未在很大程度上改变拜占庭社会总体的同质性。

en: Before we proceed to an ethnic inventory of the empire, some points of methodology are in order. Claims that Byzantium was multiethnic and multilingual can be made casually because they can be proven true with no effort whatsoever, albeit in a trivial sense. Every society of that size harbors some degree of ethnolinguistic diversity. What matters, however, is its demographic impact. It is routinely asserted, for example, that Byzantine Constantinople was a “cosmopolitan” city in which all manner of ethnicities rubbed shoulders and dozens of languages were spoken. But the proof for this assertion for the period before the influx of Latins in the twelfth century turns out to consist of prisoners of war, foreign mercenaries employed by the emperors, ambassadors, merchants passing through, and a small Muslim community, possibly also of merchants.

It is misleading to call this a “cosmopolitan” city, given that its population was in the hundreds of thousands and such groups could not have accounted for much of it. If a capital city claimed to be cosmopolitan, but its diversity consisted only of prisoners, hired guards, foreign ambassadors, and the residents of its hotels, we would not be impressed.
zh: 在我们着手编制帝国的族群清单之前，有必要先谈几点方法论。拜占庭是多族群、多语言的说法可以随口做出，因为它们毫不费力就能被证明为真，只是这样说没有多少实质意义。凡有这种规模的社会，族群和语言总会有一定的多样性。然而重要的是它的在人口结构上的分量。例如，人们惯常断言拜占庭君士坦丁堡是一座“国际都会”，各色族群摩肩接踵，数十种语言被人使用。但就十二世纪拉丁人涌入之前的时期而言，这一断言的证据原来只是战俘、皇帝雇用的外国佣兵、使节、过路商人，以及一个小型穆斯林社群（可能也是商人）。
称其为“国际都会”是误导性的，因为它的人口有数十万，而这些群体不可能占其中多大比例。如果一座都城自称国际都会，但其多样性只由囚犯、雇用的卫兵、外国使节和旅馆住客构成，也很难凭这一点就信服。

en: The Ohio State University (OSU), where I teach, has students from over a hundred countries representing dozens of ethnic groups. Yet the university is fundamentally white and Ohioan, which is how most of us here perceive it. In 2016, two-thirds of the student body were from Ohio and fewer than 20 percent were nonwhites.

It would be misleading to call this a “diverse” campus. At Rutgers University, the most diverse in the United States, only 40 percent of the student body are white, though the students are from sixty countries, fewer than at OSU.
It matters which numbers we choose to shape our impressions. OSU’s “diversity” is “truthy”: it is not actually true, but a passable impression of plausibility can be made for it.
When it appears in brochures, it is a Potemkin diversity. Something similar has been done with middle Byzantium and its capital in our scholarship.
zh: 我任教的俄亥俄州立大学（OSU）有来自一百多个国家、代表数十个族群的学生。不过，在我们这里，多数人认为这所大学主要是俄亥俄本地人的学校，也以白人为主。2016年，三分之二的学生来自俄亥俄，非白人学生不到20%。
称其为一个“多元”校园是误导性的。按这里引用的资料，在美国校园最多元的罗格斯大学，只有40%的学生是白人，尽管学生来自六十个国家，比俄亥俄州立大学还少。
我们选择哪些数字来塑造印象，这很重要。俄亥俄州立大学的“多样性”是“似真的”（truthy）：它实际上并不真实，但能营造出一种勉强说得过去的可信印象。
宣传册上出现的，是装点门面用的波将金式多样性。我们的学界对中期拜占庭及其都城也做了类似的事。

en: In most truly multiethnic empires, the dominant group is usually a small minority compared to the conquered population, which consists of many groups. Where is the balance point between a multiethnic empire on the one hand and a nation-state-with-minorities on the other? The distinction between the two is not only a matter of relative population (e.g., Roman vs. non-Roman) but also of the institutional maintenance of difference between the two in an imperial context. It would be an odd empire whose population was (say) 80 percent conquerors and 20 percent conquered, and it would also be an odd empire that extended the same rights to many of its conquered subjects as it gave to its own people.
zh: 在大多数真正多族群的帝国中，主导群体相对于由许多群体构成的被征服人口而言，通常只是少数。一端是多族群帝国，另一端是带少数族群的民族国家，两者之间的平衡点在哪里？两者的区分不仅在于相对人口（例如罗马人对非罗马人），还在于政治制度是否维持征服者与被征服者的差别。一个人口（比方说）80%是征服者、20%是被征服者的帝国会是古怪的帝国；一个把给予自己人民的相同权利扩展给许多被征服臣民的帝国，也会是古怪的帝国。

en: A second point concerns the ethnic nature of Byzantine Romanness. Evidence has already been presented in this book, and will continue to pile up, which proves that “Roman” was not a label held by or projected upon all subjects of the state collectively and indiscriminately. It was not an abstract, “umbrella identity” that could encompass Greek-speakers, Armenians, Slavs, Jews, and whoever else happened to live in territories governed by the state. Rather, it entailed specific exclusions based on language, religion, upbringing, and custom; in sum, it was an ethnicity. It is important to raise this matter again because this error is made on a regular basis by proponents of the idea that Byzantium was a multiethnic empire. For example, one scholar notes that “the empire retained its multiethnic and polyglot character—Greek-, Slav- and Armenian-speakers dominated, but other ethnic / linguistic groups counted themselves as ‘Romans’ too.”

But the sources strongly refute this formulation. If an imperial subject was sufficiently foreign as to speak primarily Slavic or Armenian, he would likely have been called a Slav or Armenian in imperial service, not a Roman. Speros Vryonis has correctly pushed back against “the often heard generalization that in Byzantium ethnic affiliation was insignificant . . . that the inhabitants of the empire felt that in effect they were all Romans and Christians.” After reviewing the evidence for the Armenians specifically, he concludes to the contrary that the Byzantines “were quite aware of ethnic distinctions among the population.”
The key difference we are looking for will not be found
the Romans but
Romans and non-Romans.
zh: 第二点涉及拜占庭罗马性的族群性质。本书已经提出、并将继续累积的证据证明，“罗马人”并不是一个国家所有臣民都可以不加区分地自称或被称作的身份。它不是一种抽象的“伞式认同”，能够涵盖说希腊语者、亚美尼亚人、斯拉夫人、犹太人，以及任何其他恰好生活在国家所治理领土上的人。毋宁说，按语言、宗教、教养和习俗划出的界线，会将一些人排除在外。概言之，这是一个族群身份。再次提出这一点很重要，因为拜占庭是多族群帝国这一观念的支持者经常犯这个错误。例如，一位学者指出：“帝国保持了其多族群、多语言的特征——说希腊语、斯拉夫语和亚美尼亚语的人占主导，但其他族群/语言群体也把自己算作‘罗马人’。”
但史料有力地驳斥了这种表述。如果一个帝国臣民与罗马人的差别大到主要使用斯拉夫语或亚美尼亚语，那么他在帝国服役时很可能被称为斯拉夫人或亚美尼亚人，而非罗马人。斯佩罗斯·弗里奥尼斯正确地反驳了“那种常听到的笼统说法：在拜占庭，族群归属无关紧要……帝国的居民觉得他们实际上都是罗马人和基督徒”。在专门审视了关于亚美尼亚人的证据之后，他得出了相反的结论：拜占庭人“相当清楚人口中的族群区分”。
我们要寻找的关键差异，不会在罗马人
找到，而是在罗马人与非罗马人

en: It is those non-Romans whom we must find in order to decide whether or not, or to what degree, Romanía was an empire. Moreover, it is not only their existence that counts but the modes in which they were governed differently by the state
they were non-Romans. Despite the occasional note of despair at ever cataloguing the empire’s ethnic groups,

this is not impossible to do. To be sure, precise figures for any part of the population lie beyond our reach, but as we have often seen, Roman sources are sensitive to ethnic difference, whether they were recording it neutrally, engaging in ethnic polemic, or elaborating literary ethnographies. It is possible to compile a kind of ethnic inventory of the Roman empire that tells us generally who lived where. It is extremely unlikely that large non-Roman groups lived in the empire without leaving any trace in the written record. We have to try, within the limitations of the available evidence, to be explicit about the empire’s alleged ethnolinguistic diversity. It can no longer be sufficient to state vaguely that it was diverse and, on that premise, classify it as a multiethnic empire without providing any documentation.

Some will no doubt insist that there was more diversity on the ground than is revealed in our sources, but this puts them in the awkward position—indeed, an untenable one—of maintaining a general and significant thesis that is unsupported by evidence. Again, the question is not whether Romanía was marked by regional diversity, as clearly it was. The question is how much of that diversity operated

that is by creating distinctions between Romans and non-Romans. It is insufficient to find that some Romans lived in the mountains whereas others lived on the plains; we must instead find non-Romans who were ruled differently from Romans.
zh: 我们必须找到的正是那些非罗马人，以便判定罗曼尼亚是否是一个帝国、或在多大程度上是一个帝国。此外，重要的不仅是他们的存在，还有国家
他们是非罗马人而对他们施行不同治理的方式。尽管偶尔有人认为不可能列清帝国有哪些族群，

但这并非不可能做到。诚然，目前还无法精确算出任何一个群体的人数，但正如我们常常看到的，罗马史料对族群差异很敏感，无论它们是中立地记述这种差异、就族群展开论战，还是以文学笔法描绘各族。有可能编制一种罗马帝国的族群清单，大致告诉我们谁住在哪里。大型非罗马群体生活在帝国中却在书面记录里不留任何痕迹，这是极不可能的。我们必须在现有证据的局限内，努力对帝国所谓的族群语言多样性做出明确说明。再也不能满足于含糊地说它是多元的，并在那一前提下、不提供任何文献证据就把它归类为多族群帝国。
无疑有些人会坚持，实际的多样性比史料所揭示的更多，但这使他们陷入尴尬的——实则是站不住脚的——境地：维护一个没有证据支持的、笼统而重大的论点。再说一次，问题不在于罗曼尼亚有无地域差异，地域差异显然存在。问题在于有多少差别是

children: 在本章所讨论的意义上

zh: 成立的，即在罗马人与非罗马人之间制造区分。仅仅发现一些罗马人住在山区而另一些住在平原是不够的；我们必须找到的是受到与罗马人不同统治的非罗马人。

en: In fact, the problem all along has not been in finding non-Roman “ethnic” types in Romanía but in finding

There are many studies of Jews, Armenians, Slavs, and others in Romanía, but the problem has been in identifying the “core group” against which they can be seen as minorities or as separate ethnic groups.

Committed to Roman denialism, historians have been unable to “see” the majority of the empire’s population, which went by the name “Roman” in the sources. Assuming wrongly that this population could not have been ethnically Roman, it has remained for us a nebulous, undefined mass of “imperial subjects” who are called “ethnolinguistically diverse.” But once we recognize them as “real” Romans, then suddenly the contours between them (the core group) and the ethnic others emerge more clearly into focus, just as they do in the sources. Thus, the question of Romanía as a multiethnic empire is but an aspect of the question of its Romanness.
zh: 事实上，考察罗曼尼亚时，历来真正难以辨认的是
。非罗马族群倒并不难找。关于罗曼尼亚的犹太人、亚美尼亚人、斯拉夫人及其他群体已有许多研究，但问题在于识别那个“核心群体”，相对于它，这些群体才能被视为少数族群或独立的族群。
由于执着于罗马否认论，史家们一直无法“看见”帝国人口的多数，而他们在史料中正是以“罗马人”之名出现的。由于错误地假定这一人口不可能是族群意义上的罗马人，学界就一直只看到一群面貌模糊、身份不明的“帝国臣民”，被称为“族群语言上多元的”。但一旦我们承认他们是“真正的”罗马人，这个核心群体与其他族群之间的界线就清晰起来，正如在史料中那样。因此，罗曼尼亚作为多族群帝国的问题，只是其罗马性问题的一个方面。

en: Our search for non-Romans must be guided by the sources. After all, discursive claims in textual sources remain the best way to establish ethnic groups and explore their history under empires. Most non-Roman groups in the empire are attested in multiple sources written in different genres, from different perspectives, and (if we are lucky) in different languages. We do not want to be at the mercy of one type of source. We must also correct for the ancient Roman convention of using pseudo-ethnic language to refer to the Roman inhabitants of a province, as well as be sensitive to changes over time. Methodologically, we are now better positioned to study ethnicity than previous scholarship ever was, especially in Byzantine Studies, which assumed that ethnic groups were fixed or inalienable. We now know that over a few generations, small and large groups could be assimilated to the dominant culture, and some of them were incentivized by the state to do so. Thus, the empire’s ethnic profile was not the same from century to century, even if there had been no intervening expansion, contraction, or influx of new settlers. We need to track not only the existence of ethnic groups but their survival or assimilation within the empire.
zh: 我们对非罗马人的寻找必须由史料引导。毕竟，要辨认具体族群并了解它们在帝国统治下的经历，最好的办法仍是读清史料对身份的说法。帝国中大多数非罗马群体，都见于以不同体裁、从不同视角、（如果我们幸运的话）用不同语言写成的多种史料。我们不想受制于单一类型的史料。我们还必须留意一种源于古罗马的惯例，即用听来像族群称谓的说法指某个行省的罗马居民。我们也要注意用语如何随时间变化。在方法论上，我们现在比以往的学界更有条件研究族群性，尤其是拜占庭研究——它曾假定族群是固定不变或无法失去的。我们现在知道，经过几代人，大小群体都可能被同化于主导文化，其中一些还受到国家的激励去这样做。因此，帝国的族群面貌一个世纪与另一个世纪并不相同，即便其间没有扩张、收缩或新移民的涌入。我们不仅需要追踪族群的存在，还要追踪它们在帝国之内的存续或同化。

en: If we place empires along a spectrum from assimilation to exclusion, all phases of Romanía would be closer to the former end of it. A recent volume on the dynamics of ancient empires links its relative homogeneity to Romanía’s extraordinary longevity as a state, correctly in my view.
zh: 如果我们把帝国沿着一条从同化到排斥的光谱排列，罗曼尼亚的所有阶段都会更靠近前者那一端。近有一部讨论古代帝国如何运作的文集，将罗曼尼亚相对同质的社会结构，同这个国家能长久延续联系起来，在我看来这是正确的。

en: The issue of [empires’] success and longevity will revolve around the same key questions: to what extent are empires of conquest able to impose upon the conquered lands and cultures their own ideological and cultural values and patterns of administration and elite formation and thereby create out of a range of different sociocultural formations a more or less homogeneous set of political values and ideological identities? Of all the “empires” discussed in this volume, the Roman—and its successor in the east Mediterranean basin, the Byzantine—states were perhaps the most successful in this respect.
zh: 要解释［帝国］为什么能成功、能延续多久，就得回答同样几个关键问题。以征服建立的帝国在多大程度上能让被征服的地方和文化接受自己的意识形态、文化价值、行政制度和造就精英的方式？它们能在多大程度上将各不相同的社会文化形态整合起来，形成大体趋同的政治价值观与意识形态认同？本书讨论的所有“帝国”中，罗马国家及其在东地中海的继承者拜占庭国家，在这方面或许最为成功。

en: The authors, Jack Goldstone (a modern political historian) and John Haldon (a Byzantinist), even wonder whether Byzantium was an empire after all, and put the word and its cognates consistently in quotation marks:
zh: 作者杰克·戈德斯通（一位现代政治史家）与约翰·哈尔顿（一位拜占庭学家）甚至怀疑拜占庭究竟是否是一个帝国，并一贯把该词及其同源词加上引号：

en: The Byzantine “empire” was, in many respects just a small, territorially unified state; its “imperial” aspect was both short lived and occasional, yet it retains the image of an empire because of its “imperial” origins, as part of the Roman imperial system.
zh: 拜占庭“帝国”在许多方面只是一个领土统一的小国；其“帝国”特征只在个别时期短暂出现。不过，它原来是罗马帝国体系的一部分，有这样的“帝国”渊源，便保留了帝国的形象。

en: This suggests that we should not be satisfied with a classification that stems from a vague “image of empire,” especially if that image (whatever its source) is not grounded in Roman realities. The sources, as we have seen, mix imperial with national Roman images of their state. The latter may have a greater claim to its enduring reality. This is what Goldstone and Haldon call “a small, territorially unified state,” not far from what I call the national state of the Romans. In fact, there is no Byzantine terminology that straightforwardly translates as “empire,” whereas the vocabulary of the Byzantine sources was full of expressions for the nation, polity, state, and monarchy “of the Romans.”
zh: 这表明我们不应满足于一种源于模糊“帝国形象”的分类，尤其当那种形象（无论其来源如何）并不扎根于罗马现实时。正如我们所见，史料把罗马国家既写成帝国，也写成罗马人的民族国家。后一个形象或许更接近这个国家长期以来的实际状况。这就是戈德斯通与哈尔顿所谓的“领土统一的小国”，与我所谓的罗马人的民族国家相去不远。事实上，没有任何拜占庭术语可以直接翻译为“帝国”，而拜占庭史料的词汇中却充满了表示“罗马人的”民族、政治共同体、国家与君主制的表达。

en: Byzantine authors sometimes reveal that their state was more expansive than just the polity of the Romans, that it had what we might call an imperial aspect. In other words, there were two ways of talking about the territory that was under Roman control: one referred to

the territory subject to the emperor, whereas the other distinguished within that territory between lands inhabited mostly by Romans (what we might call a Roman homeland) and lands inhabited mostly by foreigners (but still under imperial governance). These expressions reveal and reinforce the bounded ethnic nature of Byzantine Romanness, and would have been impossible if the latter were of “universal,” supra-ethnic scope. For example, Kekaumenos, an eleventh-century author of maxims addressing the emperor, intuitively draws a distinction between “the
of the Romans and the lands of the foreign nations
under your authority.”

He intends for these two, taken together, to refer to the entirety of what we might call the empire. In other words, not everyone under the authority of the emperor was a Roman. Previous sources can be cited to the same effect.
zh: 拜占庭作者有时透露，他们的国家比罗马人的政治共同体更为广阔，具有我们可称之为帝国性的方面。换言之，谈论罗马控制下的领土有两种方式：一种指臣服于皇帝的
领土，另一种则在那片领土之内，区分主要由罗马人居住的土地（我们可称之为罗马本土）与主要由外人居住的土地（但仍受帝国治理）。这些说法揭示并强化了拜占庭罗马身份作为一种族群身份的界线；如果后者具有“普世的”、超族群的范围，这些表达就不可能存在。例如，凯考梅诺斯——十一世纪曾撰箴言向皇帝进谏——自然而然地区分了“罗马人的
（themata）”和“陛下治下各
（ethne）的土地”。
他把这两部分合起来，指的便是我们可以称作帝国的整体。换言之，并非皇帝权威之下的每个人都是罗马人。可以引用更早的史料来达到同样效果。

en: A similar distinction is drawn in some passages written by Konstantinos VII in his survey of foreign nations around Romanía,

In one place, he refers to three forts in Armenia and says, speaking hypothetically, that “if the emperor were to hold them, a Persian army could not come against Romanía, because these forts happen to lie between Romanía and Armenia and serve as a barrier against armies.”

Therefore, what we call the empire is for him Romanía plus the foreign buffer territories. In a later passage, he distinguishes between “Romanía itself” or “Romanía proper” and some foreign forts held by the emperor.

Sources of the eleventh century also distinguish between the old Roman themes or the “Roman land” and the new “territories” that had been acquired in the recent burst of expansion. The “Roman land” strictly so called included the interior of Asia Minor but not the new territories.

This points to the recently developed theoretical concept of “the nation within the empire.” Rather than see the two concepts as polar opposites, some historians are finding that historically they often coexist, for example when one creates the other or is nestled within it.
zh: 君士坦丁七世在其关于罗曼尼亚周边外族的综述《论帝国行政》（De administrando imperio）的某些段落中，也做出了类似区分。在一处，他提到亚美尼亚的三座堡垒，并设想道：“如果皇帝占有它们，波斯军队就无法进犯罗曼尼亚，因为这些堡垒恰好位于罗曼尼亚与亚美尼亚之间，充当抵御军队的屏障。”
因此，对他而言，我们所谓的帝国就是罗曼尼亚加上外国缓冲领土。在较后的一段中，他区分了“罗曼尼亚本身”或“严格意义上的罗曼尼亚”与皇帝占有的某些外国堡垒。
十一世纪的史料也区分旧的罗马军区或“罗马土地”，与近期扩张浪潮中获得的新“领土”。严格所谓的“罗马土地”包括小亚细亚内陆，但不包括新领土。
这指向近期发展出的理论概念“帝国之内的民族”。一些史家发现，与其把这两个概念视为两极对立，不如说它们在历史上常常共存，例如当一个创造另一个、或一个包含在另一个之内时。

en: It is not clear whether this “gap” between the Roman homeland and the foreign territories was expressed through technical terminology. In two passages of the same work, Konstantinos seems to draw a distinction between “our polity
” on the one hand (i.e., that of the Romans) and “the entirety of the
(area of command or authority) of the Romans” on the other.
Perhaps this hints at a distinction between a more political mode of life for Romans domestically and a more authoritative relationship between them and their subjects. Perhaps
can be translated here as “empire,” though more research on this would be required.
Other terms could express the same idea, for example, “hegemony”: Konstantinos IX Monomachos expanded the boundaries of his
when he annexed parts of Armenia.
zh: 不清楚罗马本土与外国领土之间的这种“差距”是否通过专门术语来表达。在同一著作的两段中，君士坦丁似乎区分了“我们的政治共同体”（
，即罗马人的政治共同体）与“罗马人的全部
”（即统辖范围）。
也许这暗示了一种区分：罗马人在本土的生活更重彼此之间的政治关系，同外族臣民之间则更重命令和服从。也许
在这里可以翻译为“帝国”，尽管这需要更多研究。
其他词也能表达同样的观念，例如“霸权”：君士坦丁九世·莫诺马霍斯在吞并亚美尼亚部分地区时，扩展了他的
（霸权）的边界。

en: In this and the following chapter, I have decided to sketch the ethnic profile of Romanía at two different moments that should provide a striking contrast: the first is 930 ad, when the empire had made significant progress at absorbing some of the populations that had invaded its Balkan territories in the seventh century but before it had made any extensive conquests of its own. The second is 1064, which was the high point of imperial expansion in the whole of the empire’s history since late antiquity, not to be matched at any time afterward. Yet by 1064 Romanía had not had enough time to absorb the recently conquered populations. I will look for ethnic difference first in the provinces and then in the capital and the armies. I focus on territories of the empire administered directly by its institutions and not on various outposts and client states that recognized its authority only nominally while remaining self-governed in most ways; the empire might have been present there only by way of a court title bestowed on a local ruler. To be sure, some emperors liked to pretend that these titles literally gave them sovereignty over those client states, and sometimes even spun them into theories of world rule.

But this takes us to ideologies of symbolic empire, and not to its historical practice, which is what we are primarily interested in here. Nor do most scholars believe that such claims made specific territories part of the empire. For example, histories of Byzantium do not include histories of, say, Capua, Croatia, and Armenia. Moreover, as client states were not governed by imperial agents, the question of whether they enforced a politics of difference is moot.
zh: 在本章及下一章中，我决定勾勒罗曼尼亚在两个不同时刻的族群面貌，它们应能形成鲜明对照：第一个是公元930年，当时帝国在吸收七世纪入侵其巴尔干领土的某些人口方面已取得重大进展，但尚未自己发动大规模征服。第二个是1064年，那是自晚期古代以来帝国扩张达到的最高点，此后任何时期都无法企及。然而到1064年，罗曼尼亚还没有足够时间吸收新近被征服的人口。我将先在行省、然后在都城与军队中寻找族群差异。我聚焦于由帝国机构直接治理的领土，而非各种前哨与附庸国——它们只在名义上承认帝国权威，同时在大多数方面保持自治；帝国在那里可能仅以授予当地统治者一个宫廷头衔的方式存在。诚然，有些皇帝喜欢假装授出这些头衔就真使他们对附庸国拥有主权，有时甚至据此构想统治世界的学说。
但这把我们引向象征性帝国的意识形态，而非其历史实践，而后者才是我们这里主要关心的。大多数学者也不认为此类宣称使特定领土成为帝国的一部分。例如，拜占庭史并不包括诸如卡普阿、克罗地亚和亚美尼亚的历史。此外，由于附庸国不由帝国代理人治理，也就谈不上帝国是否在那里推行以差异为依据的统治。

en: We do not, of course, have census information and must rely on literary sources and a tiny number of documentary texts. But we are interested in groups large enough to be statistically significant, not a few clans that may have sought refuge in the mountains near the frontier. If groups had so few dealings with the Roman state or Roman society at large that they evaded attention in the sources altogether, they probably should not be included in a study of the subjects of the empire anyway. It is unlikely that larger groups altogether escaped the attention of our sources, which were quite attuned to ethnic difference. The documented survival of small minority groups in the provinces is a reassuring indicator that our source basis is not inadequate for this undertaking.
zh: 当然，我们没有人口普查信息，必须依赖叙事与文学史料及极少量的文书。但我们感兴趣的是大到具有统计显著性的群体，而非可能在边境附近山中避难的几个氏族。如果一些群体与罗马国家或广大罗马社会的往来如此之少，以至于完全避开了史料的注意，那么它们本来大概就不应被纳入对帝国臣民的研究。人数较多的群体则不太可能完全被史料忽略，因为史料对族群差异相当敏感。既然文献连行省内小规模少数族群的延续都有记载，就有理由相信现有材料可以支持这项研究。

en: The Ethnic Profile of the Provinces, ca. 930 ad
zh: 公元930年前后各行省的族群构成

en: Jews were a distinct ethnoreligious minority marked by a separate religious organization, different customs, a different national history, and the use of a different language (Hebrew) alongside the Greek vernacular. Byzantine law
proclaimed their legal equality as Roman citizens
discriminated against them as non-Christians, resulting in an incoherent legal regime that was subject to erratic ecclesiastical or imperial pressure.

The core principle was that Jews were subject to the same laws and courts as all Romans, though they were barred from high political positions and the army. But when it came to matters that pertained to their “superstition,” they were subject to the jurisdiction of their own religious leaders. Matters of purely internal concern included various contracts, marriage, and inheritance, in addition to strictly religious observances. But the Roman law of Byzantium gave Jewish women two advantages that they enjoyed nowhere else in the Jewish world: they could initiate divorce by appealing to the secular courts, and they could retain control over their own financial assets. The rabbis did not like this—and foreign rabbis were shocked that this was going on among the Roman Jews—but they were powerless to change it.

After all, “the rabbis had a vested interest . . . in viewing their version of the law of the Torah as the only legal system under which the Jews could legitimately live. This meant they regarded Roman law as basically invalid, at least for Jews.”

But individual Jews and, it seems, their women, did not agree with them all the time. So overall Jews constituted a separate nation, but they could easily integrate through conversion and even pass as Romans in some contexts without it. It is indicative that Jews from Romanía came to be known as Romaniote Jews.
zh: 犹太人是一个在族群和宗教上均有自身特征的少数群体，以独立的宗教组织、不同的习俗、不同的民族历史，以及在日常希腊语之外还使用希伯来语为特征。拜占庭法律
宣布他们作为罗马公民的法律平等，
歧视他们作为非基督徒，由此形成一种不连贯的法律体制，时而受到教会或皇帝的干预。

核心原则是犹太人与所有罗马人一样受相同法律与法庭管辖，尽管他们被排除于高级政治职位和军队之外。但涉及他们的“迷信”的事务，则受他们自己宗教领袖的管辖。只涉及社群内部的事务包括各种契约、婚姻与继承，此外还有严格的宗教仪轨。但拜占庭的罗马法律给了犹太妇女两项在整个犹太世界其他地方都享受不到的好处：她们可以通过诉诸世俗法庭主动提出离婚，并能保留对自己财产的控制。拉比们不喜欢这样——外国拉比对罗马犹太人中出现这种事感到震惊——但他们无力改变。
毕竟，“拉比们有切身利益……会把自己解释的托拉律法视为犹太人能够合法生活的唯一法律体系。这意味着他们视罗马法律为基本无效，至少对犹太人而言。”
但犹太社群中有些人，看来犹太妇女尤其如此，却并不总赞同拉比们。因此总体而言犹太人构成了一个独立的民族，但他们可以通过皈依轻易融入，甚至在不皈依的情况下有时也会被当作罗马人。一个迹象是，来自罗曼尼亚的犹太人后来被称为罗曼尼奥特犹太人。

en: Roman attitudes toward Jews were mixed. Because churchmen wrote a disproportionate number of our sources and religious texts tended to survive better than secular ones, our evidence is slanted toward theological polemic and religious hatred against the Jews. But more tolerant attitudes are attested as well. When the saint Nikon (later tenth century) wanted to expel the Jews from Sparta, a local notable, Ioannes Aratos, opposed this move. Aratos was unsuccessful, but is on record as saying that the expulsion was unjust and unreasonable.
zh: 罗马人对犹太人的态度并不一致。由于现存史料有过多出自教士之手，且宗教文本往往比世俗文本保存得更好，我们的证据偏向于针对犹太人的神学论战与宗教仇恨。但更宽容的态度也有记载。当圣尼孔（十世纪后期）想把犹太人逐出斯巴达时，当地一位显要约安尼斯·阿拉托斯反对这一举动。阿拉托斯没有成功，但史料记下了他的意见，即这种驱逐不公正，也没有道理。

en: Jews lived in many cities of the empire, and we hear of various attempts by the emperors to forcibly convert them, attempts that are reported in vague terms and never managed to eradicate Judaism from the empire. These attempts may have resulted in emigration or conversion, reducing the number of Jews in Roman society. But the community survived and grew in the phase of Roman expansion in the later tenth and eleventh centuries. This happened both through annexation and Jewish immigration from abroad.

While we cannot estimate the size of the Jewish population around 930, a Jewish traveler from Spain, Benjamin of Tudela, gives population figures for the empire’s communities around 1170 that add up to about 10,000. Inevitably, there is disagreement about how to interpret this figure (was he counting families or individuals?) and whether to accept it. Some scholars reduce the total to less than 9,000, whereas others would raise it to 75,000.
Estimates in terms of the overall size of the population of the empire range from 0.1  percent (a tenth of 1 percent) to 0.5 percent (one half of 1 percent), but such estimates are highly subjective.
At any rate, “Jews represented only a marginal element within the Byzantine population.”
They loomed larger in theological imagination than in real life.
zh: 犹太人生活在帝国许多城市，史料含糊地提到，皇帝们数次试图迫使他们改宗，且从未成功把犹太教从帝国根除。这些尝试可能导致一些人外迁或改宗，减少了罗马社会中犹太人的数量。但该社群在十世纪后期和十一世纪罗马扩张阶段存续并增长。增长既来自帝国吞并的新领土，也来自帝国之外的犹太移民。
虽然我们无法估计约930年犹太人口的规模，但一位来自西班牙的犹太旅行者图德拉的便雅悯，给出了约1170年帝国各社群的人口数字，合计约10,000。不可避免地，关于如何解读这个数字（他数的是家庭还是个人？）以及是否接受它，存在分歧。一些学者把总数降到不足9,000，另一些则会提高到75,000。
按帝国总人口来估算，犹太人口比例约为0.1%至0.5%，但此类估计高度主观。
无论如何，“犹太人在拜占庭人口中只是一个边缘成分”。
在神学论辩中，他们显得比在实际社会中重要得多。

en: Joshua Holo has masterfully drawn the complex position of the Jews in Byzantine society: “The distinct and corporate nature of the Jews readily comes through in the primary sources. . . . The minority Jews, in all their complexity, are easily identified in distinction from the majority Byzantines [as] a distinct people with its own religion, calendar and institutions. . . . To be a Jew was to belong to an ethnic group in every possible sense.”
“Byzantine Jews defined themselves in relation to their coreligionists in other countries, more than they did as subjects of the imperial state.”

Therefore, on the one hand “the Jews were not, in any modern sense, integrated; in Constantinople they lived in a separate quarter, they suffered legal limitations, and they underwent episodes of physical violence and forced baptism.” But, on the other, “the Jews defied easy dismissal as aliens or foreigners, insofar as they met a very high standard of cultural integration in signal matters of language and autochthony.”
zh: 约书亚·霍洛精妙地描绘了犹太人在拜占庭社会中的复杂处境：“从原始史料不难看出，犹太人有自己的特点，也构成一个共同体……少数族群犹太人，以其全部复杂性，很容易与多数拜占庭人区分开来，［作为］一个拥有自己宗教、历法与制度的独特民族……做一个犹太人，就是在一切可能的意义上属于一个族群。”
“拜占庭犹太人更多根据自己同其他国家犹太教徒的关系来界定自身身份，较少把自己界定为帝国臣民。”
因此，一方面“犹太人在任何现代意义上都未被融入；在君士坦丁堡他们住在一个单独的街区，遭受法律限制，并经历暴力侵害和强迫受洗”。但另一方面，“犹太人难以被轻易斥为外侨或外人，因为他们在语言和本地出身这些重要方面，已经融入当地文化很深”。

en: Jewish literature of the middle Byzantine period was written in Hebrew, though it survives mostly from southern Italy. Unfortunately, these texts have been more rigorously excluded from modern Byzantine scholarship than their authors were from contemporary Christian society. Some of these authors were clearly in dialogue with the contemporary Greek intellectual scene, though their literary productions followed separate traditions and genres and tended to assert (or presuppose) the distinctiveness of the Jewish community. This is evident, for example, in the works of Shabbatai Donnolo (tenth century) and the long family
(Ahima’as), whose partly historical and partly legendary tales cover the ninth to eleventh centuries. It is also likely that the
a Hebrew adaptation of Josephos that recounts the history of the Jewish people and was popular with medieval Jews thereafter, was also a product of Byzantine Italy.
These texts present a narrative view of Jewish national distinctiveness and would find parallels in the eleventh century in similar texts by Bulgarians and Armenians under Roman rule.
zh: 中期拜占庭时期的犹太文学用希伯来语写成，不过传下来的作品大多出自意大利南部。不幸的是，这些文本被现代拜占庭学界排除的程度，比它们的作者被当时基督教社会排除的程度还要严格。这些作者中有些显然参与了当时希腊语知识界的讨论，尽管他们的文学创作遵循独立的传统与体裁，并倾向于申言（或预设）犹太社群的独特性。例如，这在沙贝泰·多诺洛（十世纪）的作品和长篇家族《阿希玛阿斯编年史》（Chronicle of Ahimaaz，Ahima'as）中就很明显，后者半历史半传说的故事涵盖九至十一世纪。同样可能的是，《约西蓬书》（Sefer Yosippon）——一部改编自约瑟夫斯、讲述犹太民族历史、并在此后受中世纪犹太人欢迎的希伯来语作品——也是拜占庭意大利的产物。
这些文本呈现了一种关于犹太民族独特性的叙事观，十一世纪受罗马统治的保加尔人和亚美尼亚人也写下了类似的作品。

en: Armenians were among the largest minorities of non-Romans within the empire (along with Slavs, to be discussed below). As we saw in the Chapters 4 and 5, they were subject to the pull of Romanization. Some Romans had Armenian or Slavic ancestry but were not aware of the fact or not interested in it; others were (or were made) aware of this ancestry in ways that inflected their Roman ethnicity (we might call them “hyphenated Romans”); and finally there were nonassimilated Armenians or Slavs who lived in the empire or who had taken up imperial service but retained foreign cultural traits that marked them off from the mainstream of Roman society. They were perceived as foreign, though it is not entirely clear how or whether they were treated differently by the imperial state. We are here interested primarily in this last category, though it is unlikely that we will ever be able to assess its demographic impact.
zh: 亚美尼亚人是帝国内最大的非罗马人少数族群之一（与斯拉夫人并列，后者将在下文讨论）。正如我们在第4、5章所见，他们受到罗马化的吸引。一些罗马人有亚美尼亚或斯拉夫血统，但并不知道，或并不在意；另一些人自己知道这种祖源，或被别人提醒，而这样的祖源也成了他们罗马身份的一部分，可以用连字符把两种身份连在一起称呼他们；最后还有未被同化的亚美尼亚人或斯拉夫人，他们生活在帝国或已从事帝国服役，但保留着把他们与罗马社会主流区分开来的外来文化特征。他们被视为外族的，尽管不完全清楚帝国国家是否、以及如何对他们区别对待。我们这里主要对最后一类感兴趣，尽管我们不大可能有一天能够估算他们在人口中所占的比重。

en: In a study of the Byzantine aristocracy, Alexander Kazhdan concluded, based on nomenclature and biographical information, that some 10–15 percent of these families were of Armenian origin, or, in absolute terms, 30–45 out of 300.

He realized that many of them were assimilated into Byzantine society, but did not fully make the distinction between (past) ancestral origins and (present) identity. In reality, there were few officeholders who personally had foreign origin; most were two or more generations removed. There were a few Armenians from the “homeland” who rose to high positions in the Roman system, but they are found mostly in the seventh and early eighth centuries,

not the ninth and early tenth. Indeed, in the Armenian history of Ghewond, covering the seventh and eighth centuries, “fleeing to Byzantium” is presented as a regular option for the Armenian nobility. But we generally do not find ethnic Armenians in the Roman aristocracy of the tenth century.
zh: 在一项关于拜占庭贵族的研究中，亚历山大·卡日丹根据命名与传记信息得出结论：这些家族中约10%至15%出自亚美尼亚，按绝对数算就是300个家族中的30至45个。
他意识到他们中许多已同化于拜占庭社会，但没有充分区分（过去的）祖源与（当下的）认同。事实上，亲自从国外迁来并获任官职的人很少，多数人已是至少两代后的后裔。有少数来自“家园”的亚美尼亚人在罗马体制中升至高位，但他们主要见于七世纪和八世纪初，
而非九世纪和十世纪初。事实上，在格翁德涵盖七、八世纪的亚美尼亚史中，“逃往拜占庭”被呈现为亚美尼亚贵族的一条常走的出路。但我们在十世纪的罗马贵族中通常找不到族群意义上的亚美尼亚人。

en: Moreover, we should no longer postulate ethnic origins on the basis of Armenian-sounding names, as Kazhdan did, and much of the other biographical information on which such origins are postulated is, as we saw in Chapter 5, often twisted out of recognition to yield the desired result. Charanis estimated that Armenians made up about a quarter of the Roman army in the middle period, but he did so by mistaking the (huge) Armeniakon army as an ethnic Armenian army, even though the main source that he cites, Theophanes the Confessor, distinguishes between the two.
zh: 此外，我们不应再像卡日丹那样，单凭听起来像亚美尼亚语的名字便推定族群出身；而据以假定此类起源的其他传记信息，正如我们在第5章所见，常常被扭曲得面目全非，以得出想要的结果。查拉尼斯估计中期罗马军队中约四分之一是亚美尼亚人，但他这样做是把（规模庞大的）亚美尼亚军区部队误当作由亚美尼亚族人组成的部队，尽管他引用的主要史料忏悔者狄奥法尼斯区分了两者。

en: There is also no reason to believe that the statistical presence of men of Armenian origin in the aristocracy—even if that could be reliably estimated—reflected the number of Armenians living in the empire. By such Armenians I mean here not Romans of Armenian ancestry but people who could be identified as ethnically Armenian, for example those who were targeted by the stereotypes and prejudices surveyed in Chapter 5. The majority of them lived in the eastern themes, though of course we have no population figures. Modern historians sometimes give the impression that the empire’s eastern provinces throughout the middle Byzantine period were predominantly Armenian in this sense, but this is likely quite wrong and it does not correspond to the geography of Armenian history to begin with. Before the Roman conquests—so between the mid-seventh and the mid-tenth centuries—the easternmost themes closest to Armenia proper were Charsianon, Lykandos, Sebasteia, Koloneia, Mesopotamia, and Chaldia. Most of these themes were subdivisions of the original great theme of Armeniakon, with some additions of territory taken from themes to the west. By contrast, Lykandos and Mesopotamia consisted mostly of recent acquisitions (i.e., late ninth– early tenth century). Let us discuss the former group first.
zh: 即使能可靠估计贵族中有多少人出自亚美尼亚，也没有理由相信这个数字反映了帝国境内亚美尼亚族人的人数。我这里所说的这类亚美尼亚人，不是指有亚美尼亚血统的罗马人，而是指能被识别为族群意义上亚美尼亚人的人，例如第5章所考察的刻板印象与偏见所针对的那些人。他们大多数住在东部军区，当然我们没有人口数字。现代史家有时给人这样的印象：整个中期拜占庭时期，帝国东部行省主要居住着这种意义上的亚美尼亚人，但这很可能大错特错，而且它本来就与亚美尼亚历史的地理不符。在罗马征服之前——即七世纪中叶至十世纪中叶之间——最靠近亚美尼亚本部的最东端军区是哈尔西亚农、利坎多斯、塞巴斯泰亚、科洛内亚、美索不达米亚和哈尔迪亚。这些军区大多是由原先幅员辽阔的亚美尼亚军区细分而来，另加一些从西面军区划来的领土。相比之下，利坎多斯和美索不达米亚主要由新近获得的领土构成（即九世纪末至十世纪初）。让我们先讨论前一组。

en: These core territories of the theme of Armeniakon had been in Roman possession since antiquity and were ruled in the same way as other Roman territories elsewhere, although they were probably more heavily militarized. We do not have much evidence about everyday life and the nonelite population in these provinces, but their civilian and military administration, the networks of local elites, and the Church organization were all mainstream Roman (i.e., Greek-speaking and Orthodox). We have only one source that attests an Armenian population presence in these provinces. Konstantinos VII says that the theme of Koloneia in particular was mostly inhabited by Armenians.

As this occurs in a survey of the theme of Armeniakon and is followed by separate chapters on the smaller themes that were split off from it, we can tentatively conclude from his statement that Armenians were less present in the other themes.
zh: 亚美尼亚军区的这些核心领土自古代起就为罗马所有，并以与别处其他罗马领土相同的方式被统治，尽管它们可能军事化程度更高。关于这些行省的日常生活与非精英人口，我们没有太多证据，但它们的民政与军政、地方精英网络以及教会组织，都是主流罗马式的（即说希腊语、信正教）。只有一份史料提到亚美尼亚人居住在这些行省。君士坦丁七世说，科洛内亚军区尤其主要由亚美尼亚人居住。
由于这出现在对亚美尼亚军区的综述中，且随后是关于从它细分出的较小军区的独立章节，我们可以从他的说法初步得出结论：其他军区的亚美尼亚人较少。

en: This is exactly what we would expect based on the historical geography of Armenia and runs contrary to all the loose modern talk about “the Byzantine east” being populated by Armenians.

The theme of Koloneia represented the westernmost tip of ancient Lesser Armenia, which was the portion of Armenia allotted to Rome in late antiquity (the larger part had been claimed by Persia). This westernmost tip was all that Rome kept of ancient Lesser Armenia after the Arab conquests. The themes of Chaldia and Sebasteia also contained Armenian populations,

but we must also remember that by 930 these areas had been governed by Rome for almost one thousand years. Even so, “Armenian” soldiers are attested in the theme of Sebasteia in the tenth century. An expedition in 911 against the Arabs and Crete involving some 35,000 soldiers and marines of the regular army and fleet also included 1,000 Armenian cavalry from Sebasteia as well as two units of 500 Armenians from other places that cannot be precisely identified. The relative size of the numbers is telling, as is the fact that the Armenians seem to be treated as a distinctively ethnic auxiliary unit.
zh: 这正是我们根据亚美尼亚历史地理所能预期的，也与所有关于“拜占庭东部”居住着亚美尼亚人的随意现代说法相悖。
科洛内亚军区地处古代小亚美尼亚的最西端，那是古代晚期划归罗马的那部分亚美尼亚（其中较大的一部分已归波斯）。这最西端是阿拉伯征服之后罗马保有的古代小亚美尼亚的全部。哈尔迪亚和塞巴斯泰亚军区也包含亚美尼亚人口，

但我们也必须记住，到930年这些地区已被罗马统治了近一千年。即便如此，十世纪塞巴斯泰亚军区仍有“亚美尼亚”士兵的记载。911年一次针对阿拉伯人与克里特发动的远征，动用正规军与舰队约35,000名士兵与海军陆战队员，另外还有来自塞巴斯泰亚的1,000名亚美尼亚骑兵，以及来自其他无法精确识别地方的两支各500人的亚美尼亚单位。这些数字的相对规模很说明问题，亚美尼亚人似乎被当作单独编成的族群辅助部队对待这一事实也是如此。

en: In the early eighth century, Armenians in the empire may have been so few that the emperor Philippikos Bardanes (711–713) could think of expelling all of them from the empire, and he seems to have carried it out, at least against the non-Chalcedonian Armenians.
zh: 八世纪初，帝国中的亚美尼亚人可能如此之少，以至于皇帝菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯（711–713）竟想把他们全部逐出帝国，看来他也实施了驱逐，至少针对了不接受卡尔西顿会议的亚美尼亚人。

en: By contrast, Armenians made up a larger part of the population of the new but smaller militarized themes that the empire created during its expansion in the east during the tenth century. The theme of Lykandos was founded by the Armenian military entrepreneur Melias (Mleh). He found the place deserted, in the no-man’s-land between the Romans and Arabs. Under imperial patronage, he rebuilt the fort and brought in his men.

This foundation was among the earliest of the so-called small Armenian themes that began to proliferate in this region during the tenth century. As this phenomenon really picked up during the main phase of expansion, in the second half of the tenth century, we will discuss it in a later section. The nearby theme of Mesopotamia was founded in a similar way.
zh: 相比之下，在帝国十世纪向东扩张期间新建的、较小但军事化的军区中，亚美尼亚人占人口的较大部分。利坎多斯军区由组织军事拓殖的亚美尼亚人梅利亚斯（姆莱赫）建立。他发现那地方荒无人烟，处于罗马人与阿拉伯人之间的无人地带。在帝国支持下，他重建了堡垒并带入自己的人。
这是最早设立的一批所谓“小亚美尼亚军区”之一。十世纪，这类军区在本地迅速增多。由于这一现象在扩张主要阶段（十世纪后半叶）才真正加速，我们将在后面一节讨论它。附近的美索不达米亚军区以类似方式建立。

en: We do not hear of Armenian communities in central and western Asia Minor. Now, we know from many sources that larger groups had at times left Armenia for Romanía in order to escape the Arabs, or were carried off by the emperors themselves during expeditions and resettled on imperial territory, including in Thrace. A few thousand here, a few thousand there: these groups would not impact imperial demography in a major way. Moreover, they are not heard from again, suggesting that they were assimilated.

One group deserves special mention: 12,000 Armenian refugees, including women and children, fled from the Arabs and, with the permission of Konstantinos VI (780–791), entered the empire by way of the Pontos and were resettled. Some historians believe that they were resettled in the Pontos, at a place called Hemshin, and subsequently became the nucleus of the surviving ethnic group that bears that name and spoke a variant of the Armenian language. In that case, we would have a group that maintained its ethnic distinctiveness, assisted by its geographical isolation in the mountains of the Pontos. But the link between Hemshin and that specific group of refugees is tenuous.
zh: 史料没有提到小亚细亚中部和西部有亚美尼亚社群。我们从许多史料知道，有时会有较大批人从亚美尼亚迁往罗曼尼亚，以躲避阿拉伯人，或在远征期间被皇帝本人掳走、重新安置在帝国领土上，包括色雷斯。这里几千，那里几千：这些群体不会对帝国人口产生重大影响。此外，他们此后不再被提及，表明他们已被同化。
有一个群体值得特别一提：12,000名亚美尼亚难民，包括妇女和儿童，为躲避阿拉伯人而逃亡，经君士坦丁六世（780–797年在位）许可，经由本都进入帝国并被重新安置。一些史家相信他们被重新安置在本都一个叫赫姆申的地方，随后成为沿用这个名字、讲亚美尼亚语一种变体的赫姆申人的主体。那样的话，我们就有了一个保持其族群独特性的群体，本都山区的地理隔绝助长了这一点。但赫姆申与那批特定难民之间的联系是薄弱的。

en: Although “the general consensus continues to be that [Armenians] were the largest non-Greek unit of that society,”

the existence of large populations of nonassimilated Armenians is hard to document. That consensus was built, and continues to rest, on the presence of mostly assimilated elites. This has to be emphasized: in all the enthusiasm over Armenians in Byzantium, there has been no discussion of Armenian communities or populations living in the core territories the empire, so that we do not really know where or whether they existed. In modern surveys of Armenian history, medieval Armenian historians, and Roman sources, I have not found any references to Armenian populations living in the empire between the mid-seventh and the mid-tenth centuries, with the sole exception of Koloneia, mentioned by Konstantinos VII. All attention has focused on the alleged Armenian origins of the Roman aristocracy, but those origins are placed outside the empire, thus contributing to the silence about “domestic” Armenians before the period of the Roman conquests.
zh: 尽管“普遍共识仍然是［亚美尼亚人］是那个社会中最大的非希腊人群体”，

但大量未被同化的亚美尼亚人口的存在很难找到文献证据。那种共识建立在、并继续依赖于大多已同化的精英的存在之上。这一点必须强调：相关研究热衷于寻找拜占庭的亚美尼亚人，却一直未曾认真考察生活在帝国核心领土上的亚美尼亚社群或人口，以至于我们并不真正知道他们是否存在、存在于何处。在现代亚美尼亚史综述、中世纪亚美尼亚史书和罗马史料中，我没有找到任何关于七世纪中叶至十世纪中叶之间生活在帝国中的亚美尼亚人口的提及，唯一的例外是君士坦丁七世提到的科洛内亚。所有注意力都集中在罗马贵族所谓的亚美尼亚起源上，但又只追寻帝国之外的祖源，于是人们越发不谈罗马征服之前的“国内”亚美尼亚人。

en: A group related to the Armenians were the Paulicians, proponents of a religious heresy that began in Armenia, spread to Romanía, and seems (unlike most previous heresies) to have formed its own separate ethnoreligious community that broke with Romanía altogether. In the 750s, the Paulicians were regarded as still loyal enough to the empire for Konstantinos V to transfer some to Thrace to reinforce local defenses against the Bulgars.

Subsequently, in the mid-ninth century, those in Asia Minor were severely persecuted—allegedly, tens of thousands were put to death—but the operation was botched, driving many, including renegade Roman officers, to seek refuge with the Arabs in Melitene.

The Paulicians eventually established their own separate state at Tephrike and the surrounding forts, from where they launched raids into Asia Minor, sometimes collaborating with Arab raiders. Their numbers grew and the empire had to wage open war against them until they were finally defeated under Basileios I in the 870s. After the mid-ninth century, there were not many Paulicians left inside the empire. A Roman visitor to Tephrike before its capture, Petros of Sicily, reports that there were many Orthodox people living in the Paulician state as well, and that the Paulicians did not consider themselves to be Romans: they used the term “Roman” to refer to what we call Orthodoxy, and called themselves Christians. This makes them a distinct self-conscious ethnicity, which is what we would expect.
Therefore, in addition to calling them heretics (usually “Manichaeans”), the Byzantine sources call them “barbarians” in contrast to “Romans.”
zh: 与亚美尼亚人相关的一个群体是保罗派，他们信奉一宗起于亚美尼亚、后传到罗曼尼亚的异端教义，并且似乎（不像大多数先前异端那样）形成了自己独立的族群宗教社群，与罗曼尼亚彻底决裂。750年代，保罗派被认为对帝国仍足够忠诚，以至于君士坦丁五世把其中一些迁往色雷斯，以加强当地抵御保加尔人的防务。
随后，九世纪中叶，小亚细亚的保罗派遭到严重迫害——据称数万人被处死——但这场镇压事与愿违，迫使许多人（包括叛离的罗马军官）到梅利泰内的阿拉伯人那里避难。

保罗派最终在泰弗里凯及周边堡垒建立了自己独立的国家，从那里对小亚细亚发动袭掠，有时与阿拉伯袭掠者合作。他们人数增长，帝国不得不对他们发动正式战争，直到870年代在瓦西里一世治下他们最终被击败。九世纪中叶之后，帝国内部剩下的保罗派不多了。一位在泰弗里凯被攻占前到访的罗马人——西西里的彼得罗斯——报告说，保罗派国家中也生活着许多正教徒，而且保罗派不认为自己是罗马人：他们用“罗马人”一词指称我们所谓的正教信仰，而自称基督徒。这表明他们已成为有自身认同的独立族群，这正是我们所预期的。
因此，除了称他们为异端（通常是“摩尼教徒”），拜占庭史料还称他们为“蛮族”，与“罗马人”相对。

en: What became of the Paulicians after the conquest of Tephrike? The empire would not have allowed a large number of them to remain in this strategically sensitive region, so the emperor likely dispersed or exiled them, as would occur a full century later with the Muslims of Cilicia. As Petros attested, there was already an Orthodox population in Tephrike, which probably stayed in place, whereas the Paulician leadership fled to Muslim lands or Armenia.
Many rank-and-file Paulicians likely converted to Orthodoxy. A military unit of Paulicians is soon recorded as active under Roman command in southern Italy.
Some scattered groups remained in the east, for we will see below that they were moved by Ioannes I Tzimiskes to Philippopolis in Thrace, but that was after a phase of further conquest in the east.
zh: 泰弗里凯被征服后，保罗派怎么样了？帝国不会允许他们大量留在这个战略敏感地区，所以皇帝很可能驱散或流放他们，正如整整一个世纪后对基利家的穆斯林所做的那样。彼得罗斯说，当时已有一批正教徒住在泰弗里凯，他们可能留在原地，而保罗派领导层则逃往穆斯林土地或亚美尼亚。
许多普通保罗派成员很可能皈依了正教。不久就有记载，一支保罗派部队在罗马的指挥下于意大利南部行动。
一些零散群体留在东部，下文会说到，他们后来被约安尼斯一世·齐米斯凯斯迁往色雷斯的菲利波波利斯，但那是在东部进一步征服的一个阶段之后。

en: The Paulicians are an interesting, even exceptional, group in that many of them began as Romans who espoused a heresy that caused them to be viewed as non-Roman barbarians when they founded a separatist state. In 930, their numbers in the empire were small.
zh: 保罗派是一个有趣的、甚至例外的群体，因为他们中许多人起初是罗马人，信奉了一种异端，以致当他们建立一个分离主义国家时被视为非罗马的蛮族。930年，他们在帝国中的人数很少。

en: In 1929, surveying the state of the empire around 930, Steven Runciman observed that “the Asiatic population [i.e., Asia Minor] had long since been welded into a harmonious whole; but in Europe there were still undigested masses, tribes consciously distinct from, and hostile to, their neighbors and resentful of the imperial government.” In particular, he meant “the Slavs of the Peloponnese.”

In addition to the Peloponnese, the empire’s main European provinces included Greece, part of Epeiros, Thessaly, coastal Macedonia, and Thrace (beyond this line in the interior lay the Bulgarian empire). All of these territories had been invaded and settled by Slavs in the seventh century, and the empire had gradually been reestablishing control over them and absorbing them, as we saw above.

The Slavic presence was thicker in some areas than in others, though it is possible that they nowhere entirely displaced the preexisting Roman population. This was, therefore, a strange kind of “imperialism” on the part of Romanía: it was not so much expanding aggressively into a neighboring land as reclaiming its own lands and peoples who had been invaded by the Slavs. We cannot gauge the ethnic composition at this time of southern Greece, Thessaly, Macedonia, and Thrace. As we saw, Leon VI tells us that his father Basileios I converted the Slavs, taught them Greek, and made them into Romans, and their last known ethnic

date from a century before Leon. In 904, the Sklabenoi in the hinterland of Thessalonike were part of the imperial system. These are all signs that the empire was successfully assimilating them. But purely for the sake of argument, to give maximum leeway to ethnic diversity, let us hypothesize that these European territories remained 40 percent minority Slavic, possibly more Roman in southern Greece and more Slavic around Thessalonike.
zh: 1929年，史蒂文·朗西曼在审视约930年帝国状况时观察到：“亚洲人口［即小亚细亚］早已熔铸为一个和谐的整体；但在欧洲仍有未消化的群体，一些部落有意识地与邻人相区别、敌视邻人，并对帝国政府心怀不满。”他尤其指的是“伯罗奔尼撒的斯拉夫人”。
除伯罗奔尼撒外，帝国主要的欧洲行省包括希腊、伊庇鲁斯的一部分、色萨利、沿海马其顿和色雷斯（这条线之外的内陆是保加尔帝国）。所有这些领土在七世纪都曾被斯拉夫人入侵和定居，而帝国一直在逐步恢复对这些地方的控制，同时吸收当地居民，正如我们上文所见。
各地的斯拉夫居民比例并不相同，尽管他们可能在任何地方都没有完全取代既存的罗马人口。因此，这是罗曼尼亚方面一种奇怪的“帝国主义”：它与其说是咄咄逼人地扩张到邻国土地，不如说是收复自己被斯拉夫人入侵的土地与人民。我们无法衡量这一时期希腊南部、色萨利、马其顿和色雷斯的族群构成。正如我们所见，利奥六世告诉我们，他的父亲瓦西里一世使斯拉夫人皈依、教他们希腊语、把他们变成罗马人，而他们最后已知的族群
（archons）生活在利奥之前一个世纪。904年，塞萨洛尼基腹地的斯拉夫人（Sklabenoi）已是帝国体制的一部分。这些都是帝国成功同化他们的迹象。但纯粹为了论证起见，我们不妨给少数族群的比重留出尽可能大的余地，假设欧洲这些领地的居民仍有40%属于少数族群斯拉夫人。希腊南部可能罗马人较多，塞萨洛尼基周边则可能斯拉夫人较多。

en: This estimate makes greater allowance for the survival of Slavic groups as separate groups than some historians do. Judith Herrin, for example, has written that by the end of the process of assimilation Hellas was again a normal Roman province: Orthodox, Greek-speaking, and with a familiar Roman culture. The Slavs
zh: 这一估计比一些史家更宽松地估计了斯拉夫群体独立延续的可能性。例如，朱迪思·赫林写道，到同化过程结束时，希腊军区又成了一个寻常的罗马行省，居民信奉正教，讲希腊语，遵行熟悉的罗马文化。斯拉夫人

en: could not dislodge the Greek tongue or the Christian faith. Instead, the Slavs gradually embraced both, adopting in addition the medieval Byzantine style of city life (as cities slowly revived), of coinage, trading organization, ecclesiastical structure, and Hellenic culture. . . . The newcomers were converted to Christianity and inducted into Hellenic culture to become the not-always obedient subjects of the Byzantine emperors.
zh: 无法动摇希腊语或基督教信仰。相反，斯拉夫人逐渐接受了两者，此外还还在城市渐渐复兴的过程中，适应了中世纪拜占庭的城市生活，采纳了其货币、贸易组织、教会体系和希腊文化。……新来者皈依基督教、融入希腊文化，由此成了拜占庭诸帝的臣民，尽管并不总是顺从。

en: Herrin may well be right. But as I will be making a case for national homogeneity rather than “empire” in this section, I want my own subjective estimates to err in the opposite direction.
zh: 赫林很可能说得对。不过，本节将论证这里是一个大致同质的民族国家。我宁可把自己的主观估算向有利于“帝国”论的一边放宽。

en: We have slightly better indicators regarding the Peloponnese, which was a center of elite Roman culture and appears frequently in the narrative sources for this period. After 930, the only foreign “tribes” that are mentioned there are the Ezerites and Milengoi living around Mt. Taygetos, and these are who Runciman had in mind. As we saw, the Milengoi continued to have an “ethnic

” in the later tenth century. They were probably in a tributary relationship with the empire (rather than absorbed into its regular tax-surveying administration), and they still appear as a distinct group in the early thirteenth century. Otherwise we know little about them. They were almost certainly Orthodox and possibly spoke Greek, but somehow their group identity survived, the only such group in the Peloponnese who “successfully resisted assimilation.”

Still, we should make maximum allowance for ethnic diversity. For example, we do not know who lived in the remote mountains of Arcadia. I would not use the tired metaphor of an ethnic “mosaic” for the Peloponnese, certainly not for the tenth century,

but I would estimate ethnic minority groups at no more than 20 percent in the mid-tenth century. It is perhaps significant that in the lives of the saints of Greece from the ninth and early tenth centuries there is only a single solitary mention of internal barbarians, though the texts do otherwise refer to Arab raiders and other kinds of disruptive local elements.
zh: 伯罗奔尼撒的情况稍能看清一些。这里是罗马上层文化的中心，在这一时期的叙事史料中频繁出现。930年之后，那里提到的唯一外国“部落”是生活在泰格托斯山周边的埃泽里特斯人和米伦戈伊人，这正是朗西曼所想到的。正如我们所见，米伦戈伊人在十世纪后期仍有一位“族群
（doux）”。他们可能与帝国处于纳贡关系（而非被吸收进其按常规勘查地亩、登记税籍的行政体系），并且在十三世纪初仍作为一个独特群体出现。此外我们对他们知之甚少。他们几乎肯定是正教徒，可能说希腊语，但不知何故他们的群体认同存续了下来，是伯罗奔尼撒唯一“成功抵抗同化”的此类群体。
不过，我们仍应为族群多样性留出最大余地。例如，我们不知道谁住在阿卡迪亚偏远的山区。我不会对伯罗奔尼撒使用族群“马赛克”那个陈腐的比喻，尤其不会对十世纪，
但我会估计十世纪中叶少数族群占人口的比重不超过20%。也许有意义的是，在九世纪和十世纪初希腊圣徒传中，也仅有一处提到当地的蛮族，尽管这些文本在其他地方确实提到阿拉伯袭掠者和其他各种扰乱地方的成分。

en: In the seventh and eighth centuries, the emperors resettled Slavs from the Balkans to Asia Minor or allowed them to move there. Excluding military units, which are a separate category, one group was later carried off by Arab raiders;
another defected to the Arabs, and the emperor who settled them in Asia Minor (Justinian II) massacred or sold the rest into slavery;

a third group, by contrast, which fled from a war in Bulgaria to Konstantinos V and was settled at Artanas in Bithynia, on the coast, is said to have numbered 208,000, an impossible figure, especially for a group that is said to have crossed the Black Sea.
There probably were other resettled groups that are not recorded in the sources, but none were sufficiently impactful on the demography of Asia Minor as to ever be mentioned again.

It is therefore not clear that they merit a place in the ethnic profile of the tenth century, any more than do the Arab and Khurramite defectors who were also accepted and assimilated. As Rustam Shukurov recently wrote, “Byzantine authorities, as a rule, divided the immigrants into small groups and sent them to different provinces of the empire to speed up their assimilation with the local population. Usually, the immigrants, scattered in the vast expanses of the empire, lost their ethnic and religious identity by the second generation.”
zh: 七、八世纪，皇帝们把斯拉夫人从巴尔干重新安置到小亚细亚，或允许他们迁往那里。暂且不计须另作讨论的军队，其中一批人后来被阿拉伯袭掠者掳走；
另一个群体叛逃到阿拉伯人那边，把他们安置在小亚细亚的皇帝（查士丁尼二世）屠杀了其余的人或把他们卖为奴隶；
相比之下，第三个群体为躲避保加尔境内的战争，投奔君士坦丁五世，被安置在比提尼亚沿海的阿尔塔纳斯，据称有208,000人，这是一个不可能的数字，尤其对于一个据称渡过黑海的群体而言。
可能还有其他未被史料记载的重新安置群体，但这些群体对小亚细亚人口构成的影响看来不大，史料也没有再提到他们。
因此不清楚他们是否值得在十世纪族群面貌中占有一席之地，正如那些同样被接纳和同化的来投的阿拉伯人和胡拉米派信徒一样。正如鲁斯塔姆·舒库罗夫近期所写：“拜占庭当局通常把移民分成小群体，送往帝国不同行省，以加速他们与当地人口的同化。通常，散布在帝国广袤土地上的移民，到第二代就丧失了其族群与宗教认同。”

en: A case in point are the Bulgars. A number of them defected along with their families under Michael I (811–813) and were resettled “in various areas” of the empire.
Presumably there were other such groups. Some Bulgarians are attested in 959 in a village near Mt. Athos.

But that is all we can say safely about Bulgarians in the empire of 930. The eleventh-century vita of Lazaros of Galesion mentions a village near Ephesos called Boulgarin, from which some scholars deduce the presence of Bulgarians, though the text says nothing about that when the protagonist meets its inhabitants. Even if they were Bulgarians, they may have been settled there by Basileios II after his conquest of Bulgaria (he regularly moved conquered subjects around).
zh: 一个恰当的例子是保加尔人。他们中一些人在米海尔一世（811–813）治下携家眷投奔帝国，被重新安置在帝国“各地区”。
想必还有其他此类群体。959年，阿索斯山附近一个村庄有保加尔人的记载。
但关于930年帝国中的保加尔人，我们能稳妥说的仅此而已。十一世纪的《加莱西翁的拉扎罗斯传》提到以弗所附近一个叫布尔加林的村庄，一些学者据此推断有保加尔人存在，尽管文本在主人公遇见村民时对此只字未提。即便他们是保加尔人，也可能是瓦西里二世在征服保加尔帝国之后把他们安置在那里的（他经常迁移被征服的臣民）。

en: Another interesting theory concerns Saint Ioannikios (ca. 760–846 ad) and the Roman family of Boïlas (plural: Boïlades). Ioannikios began as a soldier in the Roman army and was present at the battle of Markellai (792), a Bulgar victory, after which he turned to the religious life. During the battle, the future saint encountered the emperor, who asked him who he was. Ioannikios replied, “I am from the province of Bithynia, from the village of Marykaton and the family of Boïlas; my name is Ioannikios, and I am an
in rank.”

The name Boïlas is a Greek rendition of a Bulgar noble rank. It is a stretch to conclude from this alone that Ioannikios himself was biologically descended from resettled Bulgars, but it is not impossible. Vryonis, who proposed the theory, concluded that their “assimilation . . . seems to have been rapid and complete,” facilitated by the Church and the army.
Ioannikios’ parents were Christians, and as a Roman soldier he fought against the Bulgars (who, at the time, were not Christians).
zh: 另一个有趣的理论涉及圣约安尼基奥斯（约公元760–846）和罗马的博伊拉斯家族（复数：博伊拉德斯）。约安尼基奥斯起初是罗马军队中的一名士兵，参加过保加尔人取胜的马尔凯莱战役（792），后来转而修行。战斗中，这位未来的圣徒遇见了皇帝，皇帝问他是谁。约安尼基奥斯回答：“我来自比提尼亚行省，来自玛丽卡通村和博伊拉斯家族；我叫约安尼基奥斯，军衔是
（exkoubitor，宫廷卫兵）。”
博伊拉斯这个名字是保加尔贵族头衔的希腊语转写。仅凭这一点就断定约安尼基奥斯确为那批迁来的保加尔人的血缘后裔，是牵强的，但并非不可能。提出这一理论的弗里奥尼斯得出结论：他们的“同化……似乎迅速而彻底”，由教会与军队促成。
约安尼基奥斯的父母是基督徒，而作为一名罗马士兵，他与保加尔人作战（他们当时还不是基督徒）。

en: Groups of Syrian Orthodox (Jacobites) were taken in three raids in the eighth century and resettled in Thrace (once with some Armenians too, who included Paulicians in their midst).
At this time, the members of the Syrian Church were becoming a separate ethnicity,

so initially at least they might have formed an ethnoreligious minority in Thrace. Some would have resisted conversion to Byzantine Orthodoxy, but we do not know for how long. The first of these three groups is said to have survived until the early eighth century, so for fifty or sixty years, but they are not attested after that. (They would become much more important after the imperial expansion of the later tenth century, as we will see in Chapter 7.)
zh: 八世纪的三次袭掠中掳来的叙利亚正教（雅各派）群体被重新安置在色雷斯（有一次还带着一些亚美尼亚人，其中夹杂保罗派）。
这一时期，叙利亚教会的成员正在成为一个独立的族群，
所以至少最初他们可能在色雷斯构成一个在族群和宗教上都有自身特征的少数群体。有些人会抵抗皈依拜占庭正教，但我们不知道持续了多久。这三个群体中的第一个据称存续到九世纪初，即五六十年之久，但此后不再有记载。（他们将在十世纪后期帝国扩张之后变得重要得多，正如我们将在第7章看到的。）

en: It was in southern Italy that the empire’s presence was most imperial in nature; that is where the management of ethnic differences was a central feature of provincial administration. Two provinces were reconstituted in the ninth century, Calabria and Longobardia (i.e., Apulia). Although they were governed almost as regular themes by governors and armies sent from Constantinople, they “represented too different and too distant a world to be directly relevant to the history of the central lands of the empire.”

Italy highlights by contrast how homogeneous the central lands were. But it would be special pleading to exclude it from this survey. Unfortunately, the Greek sources pay little attention to Italy and so it is difficult to talk about their perception of local ethnicities. The

of Leon VI says that when the general Nikephoros Phokas was sent in the 880s to subdue Calabria his operations at least in part targeted “the nation of the Lombards,” whom he subdued and made to feel “free from all slavery” by not imposing high taxes on them.
In another text, this act is called “restoring them to the former sovereignty of the Roman
Even so, they are represented as a distinct ethnic group.
zh: 正是在意大利南部，罗马统治最接近帝国的形态，因为按族群差别施政是当地行省行政的核心。九世纪重建了两个行省：卡拉布里亚和伦巴第（即阿普利亚）。尽管它们几乎像常规军区一样由君士坦丁堡派出的总督和军队治理，但它们“代表了一个太过不同、太过遥远的世界，与帝国中心土地的历史没有直接关联”。
意大利通过对照凸显了中心土地是多么同质。但把它排除在这项考察之外就难免有偏袒之嫌。不幸的是，希腊史料很少关注意大利，因此很难谈论它们对当地族群的看法。利奥六世的《战术》（Taktika）说，880年代将军尼基弗鲁斯·福卡斯被派去制服卡拉布里亚时，他的行动至少部分针对“伦巴第民族”，他制服了他们，并通过不向他们征收重税让他们觉得自己“摆脱了一切奴役”。
在另一文本中，这一行为被称为“使他们重新接受此前罗马
（统辖区域）的统治”。
即便如此，他们仍被呈现为一个独特的族群。

en: The documentary evidence from these provinces indicates that Calabria had a large Greek-speaking population, whereas in Apulia the majority was Lombard or Latin Italian, so overall there was a significant Latin-rite presence. By 930, the Churches of Rome and Constantinople had not yet decided to insist on their differences to the point of schism. The non-Greek population of these provinces was allowed to live according to its own customs and follow Lombard laws, an arrangement with few parallels in the rest of the empire. For example, the legal status of women was different within their respective two communities. Administrative personnel sent from the center formed a thin layer in Apulia that ruled through the cooperation of Lombard notables, some of whom bore the non-Roman title of

A visitor from the core lands of Romanía would have found in southern Italy the greatest diversity, regimented by language or ethnic categories. There were also Jewish communities, as elsewhere throughout the empire, which used Hebrew for some purposes (e.g., tombstones).

The fiscal documents of the churches and monasteries of these provinces, which are mostly in Latin, sometimes classify individuals by their language or ethnicity. They can refer, for instance, to a Greek, Armenian, Jew, and (later) a Norman.
A privilege in Latin given by an imperial official to the monastery of Montecassino gives an ethnic inventory of people in imperial service in the region: “Armenians, Greeks, and Lombards.”
Many deeds are explicitly executed according to the “laws” or the “customs” of the Lombards.
As it was not the purpose of  those documents to provide ethnological information, these glimpses provide valuable evidence for wider social perceptions of ethnicity.
zh: 这些行省的文书证据表明，卡拉布里亚有大量说希腊语的人口，而在阿普利亚多数是伦巴第人或拉丁意大利人，因此总体上有相当多的居民遵循拉丁礼。到930年，罗马与君士坦丁堡教会尚未决定坚持分歧到分裂的地步。这些行省的非希腊人口被允许按自己的习俗生活、遵循伦巴第法律，这种安排在帝国其余地方很少见。例如，妇女在各自两个社群内的法律地位不同。从中心派出的行政人员人数不多，在阿普利亚要靠伦巴第地方显贵的合作来维持统治，其中有些人带有非罗马的
（gastald）头衔。
一位来自罗曼尼亚核心土地的访客，会在意大利南部发现最为多样的人群，他们按语言或族群接受不同的管辖。也有犹太社群，正如帝国其他地方一样，它们在某些用途上使用希伯来语（例如墓碑）。
这些行省教会与修道院的财政文书大多用拉丁语，有时按语言或族群对个人分类。例如，它们可能提到一个希腊人、亚美尼亚人、犹太人，以及（后来的）诺曼人。
一位帝国官员用拉丁语授予蒙特卡西诺修道院的一份特权状，给出了该地区帝国服役人员的族群清单：“亚美尼亚人、希腊人和伦巴第人。”
许多契约明确按照伦巴第人的“法律”或“习俗”订立。
