由于那些文书的目的不是提供民族学信息，这些偶然留下的记载，有助于了解当时社会如何划分不同人群。

en: We have little evidence about how the “Greek” minority in southern Italy perceived itself. We cannot say for certain that they called themselves Romans, though that is by no means to be ruled out.

A tenth-century Jewish scholar in Byzantine Italy, Shabbatai Donnolo, who knew Greek, Latin, and Hebrew, referred to his life in lands “under the Romans’ rule,” suggesting that the term had local valence.
But local terminology may have also been shaped by the linguistic habits of the Latinate majority, making it possible that the Greek-speakers there called themselves
(in Greek). We must also be careful because Latin texts could at times subsume various ethnic groups from the east under the lump linguistic term

Moreover, the proximity of the city of Rome and the presence there of a “Roman” community distinct from that of Romanía would have complicated the local use of the typical Byzantine terminology of “Romans” and “others.”

The southern Italian context was tricky, caught as it was between rival linguistic taxonomies. But the Greek-speakers, who would be “Romans” in the core territories, definitely perceived themselves as ethnically different from the Latin majority. When Neilos, from Rossano in Calabria, traveled to Rome, he lodged in a monastery of “men from the same race as himself,” that is, of Greek-speakers.
zh: 关于南意大利的“希腊”少数群体如何看待自身，我们几乎没有证据。我们无法确定他们是否自称罗马人，尽管这绝非不可能。
十世纪拜占庭意大利的一位犹太学者沙贝泰·多诺洛通晓希腊语、拉丁语与希伯来语，他提到自己生活在“罗马人统治之下”的土地上，可见这个称谓在当地为人所知。
但当地用语也可能受到占多数的拉丁语群体语言习惯的塑造，使得那里的希腊语使用者有可能自称
（希腊语“希腊人”）。我们还须谨慎，因为拉丁文本有时会把来自东方的各种族群归并到
（拉丁语“希腊人”）这一笼统的语言标签之下。
此外，罗马城近在咫尺，那里存在一个有别于罗曼尼亚的“罗马”共同体，这会使当地对“罗马人”与“他者”这套典型拜占庭用语的使用变得复杂。
南意大利的语境很棘手，因为它希腊语与拉丁语各有一套划分人群的用语，在这里难以一一对应。但那些在核心领土上会被视为“罗马人”的希腊语使用者，无疑认为自己在族群上不同于拉丁多数群体。当来自卡拉布里亚罗萨诺的圣尼洛斯前往罗马时，他住进了一所由“与他同族之人”居住的修道院，也就是希腊语使用者的修道院。

en: A final oddity remains to be mentioned. Konstantinos VII notes the existence of a group living on the very tip of the Mani peninsula (of the Peloponnese) who were called Hellenes by the locals, not because they were descended from the ancient Greeks—Konstantinos says specifically that they were descended from “the ancient Romans”—but because they remained pagans until the reign of his grandfather Basileios I (867–886). Yet they continued to be called Hellenes even after their conversion to Christianity. Moreover, they appear not to have been fully integrated into the imperial administration as they received an
from the local general
a policy that was used for nonassimilated groups. Konstantinos’ solitary mention of this group has fueled more speculation than it can bear.

Unfortunately, we do not know how this group saw itself. Whatever its nature, it was seen by him as standing outside the mainstream. Now, for the Romans of Byzantium a “Hellene” was one of two things: an ancient Greek or a pagan regardless of ethnicity. The group in the Peloponnese may have actually been descended from ancient Greeks, but that is not how Konstantinos and their local neighbors saw them: they saw them as descended from the ancient Romans and called them Hellenes because of their religion.

At any rate, by the eleventh century, the Mani presents an Orthodox profile with a dense cluster of newly built churches. We know a stoneworker active in the southwestern Peloponnese who carved his name on his productions (“Niketas”), in one case adding “from the country of Mani.”
zh: 还有一个奇特之处尚待提及。君士坦丁七世指出，在（伯罗奔尼撒的）马尼半岛最南端住着一群人，被当地人称为希腊人（Hellenes），不是因为他们源自古希腊人——君士坦丁明确说他们源自“古罗马人”——而是因为他们直到其祖父瓦西里一世（867–886）在位时仍是异教徒。然而即便在他们皈依基督教之后，仍继续被称为希腊人。此外，他们似乎并未完全融入帝国行政体系，因为当地
（strategos）为他们任命了一位
（archon），这是用于未同化群体的政策。君士坦丁只在这一处提到这个群体，却引出了远非这则孤证所能支持的猜测。
遗憾的是，我们不知道这一群体如何看待自身。无论其性质如何，在他看来它都立于主流之外。对拜占庭的罗马人而言，“希腊人”（Hellene）有两层意思：古希腊人，或不论族群的异教徒。伯罗奔尼撒的这一群体或许确实源自古希腊人，但君士坦丁与他们当地的邻居并不这样看：他们认为他们源自古罗马人，并因其宗教而称他们为希腊人。
无论如何，到十一世纪，马尼呈现出正教面貌，新建教堂密集簇集。我们知道一位活跃于伯罗奔尼撒西南部的石匠，他在自己的作品上刻下名字（“尼基塔斯”），有一次还加上“来自马尼之地”。

en: That, in outline, is the ethnic profile presented by the main territories of the empire around 930 ad. I have generally excluded client states, outposts, small groups that are not reliably attested as still surviving in the tenth century or that were not ethnoreligiously different from the Roman majority, as well as ethnic monasteries, which were religious outposts of foreign groups.

A single example can demonstrate that perceptions of ethnicity governed these groups as well. When the Georgian monk Hilarion (ninth century) and his followers traveled to the monastic center of Mt. Olympos in Bithynia, they were treated with suspicion by some of the local monks because of their foreignness; note that the Georgians were, from the Byzantine point of view, perfectly Orthodox. After Hilarion’s death, the emperor Basileios I wanted to give a monastery in Thessalonike to his disciples but they refused on the grounds that it would not be appropriate for a monastery to be taken away from the natives “and given to us, who are foreign men.”
Orthodoxy was united by faith but riven by ethnicity.
zh: 以上大致就是约公元930年帝国主要领土呈现的族群面貌。我一般排除了附庸国、前哨、没有可靠证据表明在十世纪仍存续或在族群宗教上不同于罗马多数群体的小群体，以及由特定族群所办的修道院，这些修道院是外族在外地的宗教据点。
一个例子就能表明，人们对族群差别的看法同样影响这些群体。当格鲁吉亚修士希拉里翁（九世纪）及其追随者前往比提尼亚的奥林波斯山修道中心时，他们因外族身份而受到一些当地修士的猜疑；请注意，从拜占庭的观点看，格鲁吉亚人是完全正教的。希拉里翁死后，皇帝瓦西里一世想把塞萨洛尼基的一所修道院赐给他的门徒，但他们拒绝了，理由是把修道院从本地人手中夺走“并交给我们这些外邦人”并不合适。
共同信仰将正教徒联系起来，族群界线又把他们分隔开来。

en: Constantinople and the Army
zh: 君士坦丁堡与军队

en: Byzantine Constantinople is routinely called a multiethnic, even a cosmopolitan, city—indeed, a “mosaic”—and the Byzantine armies are also said to have been multiethnic. Both of these impressions are wrong.
zh: 拜占庭的君士坦丁堡常被称作多族群的城市、甚或一座由各族拼成的“马赛克”式国际都会，拜占庭军队也被说成是多族群的。这两种印象都是错误的。

en: First, a note on demography. In 930, Constantinople may have had a population of around 250,000,

and the nominal strength of the empire’s armies may have been around 150,000 men. If the empire’s total population was around 10 million, then the first represented 2.5 percent of the total while the second was 1.5 percent. Yet for all that they were small, these two sites of Romanness were disproportionately powerful in relation to their size. They appear frequently in the sources and were often regarded as stand-ins for the empire as a whole, by both medieval and modern writers.
zh: 先谈一点人口状况。930年，君士坦丁堡的人口可能约为25万，
而帝国军队的名义兵力可能约为15万人。若帝国总人口约为1000万，那么前者占总人口的2.5%，后者为1.5%。然而尽管规模小，都城和军队是罗马身份如此突出的两个场所，影响力与所占人口的比重并不相称。它们频繁出现在史料中，且无论中世纪还是现代的作者，都常以它们代表整个帝国。

en: Our image of Constantinople as home to a number of ethnic or religious communities comes from the later Byzantine period and especially the Ottoman period. During the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, Italian cities such as Venice and Genoa established outposts there that functioned as “branch offices” of their polities back home, confined to specific locations (see below). We also know from the Spanish Jewish traveler Benjamin of Tudela (1170s) that Constantinople’s Jews had their own “quarter.” Specifically, there were two thousand Rabanite Jews and five hundred Karaite Jews, both required to live in Pera, across the Golden Horn, but they so disliked each other that they had built a wall between them.

It is debatable whether such segregation counts as cosmopolitanism, but here we are interested more in numbers and presence. The City’s diversity, meaning the number and size of its ethnic enclaves, grew during the later Byzantine period and exploded under the sultans. But what was it in 930?
zh: 我们把君士坦丁堡想象为若干族群或宗教社群的家园，这一印象来自拜占庭晚期，尤其是奥斯曼时期。十二、十三世纪，威尼斯与热那亚等意大利城市在那里设立据点，宛如各自城邦在当地的“分支机构”，各据特定地段（见下文）。我们还从西班牙犹太旅行家图德拉的便雅悯（1170年代）那里得知，君士坦丁堡的犹太人拥有自己的“街区”。具体而言，有两千名拉班派犹太人与五百名卡拉派犹太人，两者都被要求住在金角湾对岸的佩拉，但他们彼此极为厌恶，竟在中间筑了一道墙。
分区而居是否足以称得上国际都会，尚可争论。这里更关心当时有哪些社群，人数有多少。都城的多样性，即其族群飞地的数量与规模，在拜占庭晚期增长，并在苏丹治下激增。但930年时的情况如何？

en: We can certainly assume a Jewish presence.

Beyond that, as noted above, studies of Byzantine Constantinople list under the category of cosmopolitanism prisoners of war, foreign mercenaries, foreign ambassadors, itinerant merchants, and a small Muslim community.

However, none of these groups were certainly natives of the City. At some point, the Muslims (mostly Arabs) were allowed to have a mosque, the object of negotiation between the emperors and various Muslim powers who acted as the patrons or sponsors of the City’s Muslims. The latter cannot have been more than a few hundred, but their existence is at least documented. However, there is no definitive evidence that this group contained more than prisoners of war (some of them of high rank and so treated well by the Roman authorities), envoys, and merchants, some of whom apparently resided in the City for ten years or more.

There is no other evidence for foreign or ethnic communities. For example, no Armenian community has been identified in the sources, though we know that notables came to settle there from Armenia on an individual basis or in small groups. Some of them were important enough to be given manors by the emperors, and they brought their families and retinues with them.

But it does not seem that they formed a coherent ex-patriot community, and these types of immigrants assimilated quickly. They were quite unlike the Italian colonies that built up in Constantinople in the twelfth century.
zh: 我们当然可以假定有犹太人存在。
除此之外，如上所述，关于拜占庭君士坦丁堡的研究以如下人群证明它是一座国际都会战俘、外国雇佣兵、外国使节、行商以及一个小型穆斯林社群。
然而这些群体究竟有没有在当地出生的人，并不能确定。某个时候，穆斯林（多为阿拉伯人）获准拥有一座清真寺，这是皇帝与各穆斯林势力之间谈判的对象，后者充当都城穆斯林的庇护者或支持者。城里的穆斯林不会超过几百人，但其存在至少有文献可证。然而没有确凿证据表明这一群体包含战俘（其中一些地位很高，因而受到罗马当局优待）、使节与商人之外的其他人，这些商人中有些显然在都城居住了十年或更久。
此外，再无证据显示有其他外国侨居社群或少数族群社群。例如，史料中没有发现有组织的亚美尼亚社群，尽管我们知道有显贵以个人或小群体形式从亚美尼亚来此定居。他们中有些地位显赫，甚至得到皇帝赐予的庄园，并携家眷与扈从同来。
但他们似乎并未形成一个凝聚的侨居社群，这类移民同化得很快。他们与十二世纪在君士坦丁堡形成的意大利侨居地截然不同。

en: It is likely that there were more foreigners in Constantinople than our sources reveal, though unlikely that demographically significant groups have passed completely unnoticed. For example, it is only by a chance reference in Liudprand of Cremona, a western bishop who traveled on official business to Constantinople, that we know of some Amalfitans, Gaetans, and Romans (from Rome) there in 945 and even of some Latin beggars in 968.

Liudprand says that the authorities in Constantinople, who were hostile to him, seized those beggars and did not allow them to approach him. There is another chance reference to a Khazar living in, or passing through, tenth-century Constantinople.
zh: 君士坦丁堡的外国人很可能比史料实际记下的更多，但人口规模显著的群体不太可能完全未被注意。例如，只是凭借克雷莫纳的利乌特普兰德——一位因公务前往君士坦丁堡的西方主教——的一处偶然提及，我们才知道945年那里有一些阿马尔菲人、加埃塔人与罗马人（来自罗马城），甚至968年还有一些拉丁乞丐。
利乌特普兰德说，对他怀有敌意的君士坦丁堡当局扣押了那些乞丐，不让他们接近他。另有一则偶然留下的记载，说有一名哈扎尔人居于十世纪的君士坦丁堡，或是从那里经过。

en: In general, the movement of foreigners seems to have been subject to rigorous restrictions. A treaty of around 907 with the Rus’ stipulated where their merchants visiting the City could stay and for how long; they could enter only in small groups whose names were recorded.
“The activities of foreign merchants . . . were regulated and controlled.”
This was not an “open city.” Soldiers guarded the major crossroads inside, patrolled the City at night, and arrested people who were out and about.
A number of saints who looked odd or had spent time abroad and so looked like foreigners were arrested as spies when they approached Roman cities.

For example, in the tenth century Basileios the Younger got into trouble because he was acting weirdly and wearing foreign clothes: he was arrested in Asia Minor and taken in chains to the capital for interrogation.
The story may be fictitious but reveals contemporary perceptions and possibly policies.
zh: 总体而言，外国人的流动似乎受到严格限制。约907年与罗斯人签订的一项条约规定了来访都城的商人可以住在何处、停留多久；他们只能以小群体形式进入，且名字须登记。
“外国商人的活动……受到约束和管制。”
这不是一座“开放城市”。士兵把守城内主要路口，夜间在都城巡逻，逮捕在夜间外出走动的人。
一些相貌怪异、或曾在国外逗留因而看起来像外国人的圣徒，在接近罗马城市时被当作间谍逮捕。
例如十世纪时，小圣瓦西里因举止怪异、穿着外国服装而惹上麻烦：他在小亚细亚被捕，被锁链押送到首都审讯。
这个故事或许是虚构的，却能让人看到时人的观念，或许也透露了当时的政策。

en: Let us turn from the City to the army. The emperors of Romanía were, at times, wealthy enough to hire thousands of foreign soldiers and mercenaries. Their armies were often mocked by enemies for consisting of a medley of various ethnicities with no cohesion or patriotic morale.

But these caricatures were true only in unusual circumstances, and we should not rely on their image of the Roman armies as a “mosaic” of nations. In the middle Byzantine period before 1081, soldiers were recruited overwhelmingly among Romans in the provinces; there was an elaborate system for doing so.
In fact, all but a tiny fraction were Roman recruits. The Byzantine sources regularly distinguish between Roman soldiers and “ethnics

though sometimes the Romans are listed by province, which should not confuse us: Macedonians, Cappadocians, and the like were just provincial Roman units. When the system of indigenous recruitment began to break down in the 1060s, we hear about it. A historian says that when the emperor Konstantinos X Doukas (1059–1067) needed to assemble an army in a hurry and under pressure, he did so “not in a manner that was fitting for an emperor of the Romans, but only in the way allowed by circumstances, including Macedonians, Bulgarians, Cappadocians, Ouzes, and the other foreigners who happened to be present, in addition to the Franks and Varangians.”
zh: 让我们从都城转向军队。罗曼尼亚的皇帝有时足够富有，能雇佣数千外国士兵与雇佣兵。他们的军队常被敌人嘲笑为由各族群拼凑的大杂烩，缺乏凝聚力或爱国士气。
但这些夸张的讽刺描绘只在特殊情况下才属实，我们不应依赖它们把罗马军队想象成各族的“马赛克”。在1081年以前的拜占庭中期，士兵绝大多数从行省的罗马人中征募；为此有一套精密的制度。
事实上，除了极少数例外，士兵都是从罗马人中招募的。拜占庭史料经常区分罗马士兵与“异族”（
尽管有时罗马人按行省列出，这不应使我们困惑：马其顿人、卡帕多西亚人之类只是行省罗马部队。十一世纪六十年代，本土征兵制度逐渐瓦解，史料也留下了记载。一位史家说，当皇帝君士坦丁十世·杜卡斯（1059–1067）迫于形势急须集结军队时，他这样做“不是以适合罗马人皇帝的方式，而只是以情势所允许的方式，包括马其顿人、保加尔人、卡帕多西亚人、乌泽人，以及其他恰好在场的外国人，此外还有法兰克人与瓦良格人”。

en: Ethnic units were recruited in small numbers for their specialized skills or in order to enforce treaty obligations.

Such units typically included fewer than 1,000 men, though they tended to be used more heavily in actual operations: an expedition would be likely to include a higher proportion of foreign soldiers than did the paper strength of the armed forces as a whole.
zh: 罗马只招募少量外族部队，看重的是他们的专门技能，或是要使条约中规定的义务得到履行。
这类部队通常少于一千人，实战中却往往更频繁地动用他们。因此，远征部队中的外族士兵比例，很可能高于他们在全军名义编制中所占的比重。

en: Consider two surviving inventories of soldiers, pay, and equipment that relate to the expeditions against the Arabs and Crete in 911 and 949. These texts present complex problems of interpretation, but these affect our understanding of Byzantine accounting more than the numbers of foreign soldiers.

For the expedition of 911, the text stipulates 700 Rus’ auxiliaries in the fleet and 2,000 Armenian cavalry from Sebasteia and other themes to join a Roman army numbering perhaps 35,000; there would also be 5,087 Mardaïtes of the west (see below for them).

For the expedition of 949, whose overall size was between 20,000 and 30,000, the fleet was to include 629 Rus’ (in nine of their ships), 368 Dalmatians, and 3,000 Mardaïtes; and the cavalry would include 1,000 recently enlisted Armenians from the east (i.e., the eastern themes) and 220 Sthlabesianoi (Slavs) from the Opsikion theme.

The true foreigners here were only the Rus’, while the Dalmatians came from nearby client states. The Armenians were likely domestic ethnic minorities. The two other groups require some explanation, but we can already see that this was an “OSU” level of diversity: many ethnic names in a row, but small numbers.
zh: 来看两份存世的士兵、军饷与装备清单，它们涉及911年与949年针对阿拉伯人与克里特的远征。这些文本带来复杂的解读问题，但这些问题更影响我们怎样理解拜占庭的军费账目，对外族士兵人数的理解影响较小。
就911年远征而言，账册列出舰队中的700名罗斯辅助兵，以及从塞巴斯泰亚等军区调来的2,000名亚美尼亚骑兵，他们加入的是一支人数可能达35,000人的罗马大军；此外还有5,087名西部马尔达伊特人（关于他们见下文）。
就949年远征而言，其总规模在2万至3万之间，舰队须包括629名罗斯人（乘他们自己的九艘船）、368名达尔马提亚人和3,000名马尔达伊特人；骑兵则包括1,000名新近入伍、来自东方（即东部军区）的亚美尼亚人，以及来自奥普西基翁军区的220名斯拉维西亚诺伊人（Sthlabesianoi，即斯拉夫人）。
这里真正的外国人只有罗斯人，而达尔马提亚人来自邻近附庸国。亚美尼亚人很可能是帝国境内的少数族群成员。另外两个群体需要一些解释，但我们已能看出这是一种俄亥俄州立大学式的“多样性”：一连串族群名称，但人数很少。

en: Some ethnonyms occur exclusively in connection with military units. The Sklabesianoi (spelled variously) were units of Slavs stationed in Asia Minor, mostly in the Opsikon theme, from where they could be dispatched to trouble areas throughout the empire or beyond. They may have had a Slavic ethnicity (whatever that looked like), for the emperor Romanos I Lakapenos was eager to settle an uprising of the “Slavs” in the Peloponnese (i.e., the Milengoi and the Ezerites) before they could join forces with some “Slavesians” who were causing trouble there too. Be that as it may, the Sthlabesianoi are attested only for the half century 911–961, and cannot have numbered more than a few hundred.
zh: 有些族名只用来称呼某些部队。斯拉维西亚诺伊人（Sklabesianoi，拼写各异）是驻小亚细亚的斯拉夫人部队，多在奥普西基翁军区，可从那里被派往帝国各地乃至境外的动乱地区。他们可能仍有斯拉夫族群身份，尽管这种身份具体是什么样并不清楚，因为皇帝罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯急于平息伯罗奔尼撒“斯拉夫人”（即米伦戈伊人与埃泽里特斯人）的一场起义，以免他们与同样在那里制造麻烦的一支“斯拉维西亚诺伊人”（Slavesians）合流。无论如何，斯拉维西亚诺伊人（Sthlabesianoi）仅在911–961这半个世纪有记载，人数不可能超过几百。

en: The Mardaïtes (called Jarajima in Arabic) appear immediately after the Arab conquests as a martial Christian group inhabiting the Amanos mountains, between Cilicia and Syria. They helped the emperors against the Arabs but were basically autonomous, until Justinian II made a deal with the caliph around 687 and resettled 12,000 of them in the empire.

Scholars have debated the ethnic origin of the Mardaïtes but the sources give no clear indication; they appear to have been a mixed group that effectively constituted their own new identity. They were dispersed to the naval themes of Asia Minor and Greece, where they are attested in the ninth and tenth centuries, serving as oarsmen. The expedition of 911 included 5,087 Mardaïtes of the west, whereas that of 949 included 3,000.
Their captain in the Kibyrraiotai theme (Attaleia) seems not to have been under the direct orders of the local military governor and was appointed directly by the emperor.

It is not clear what kind of group the Mardaïtes constituted after they entered Roman service. They were Christian to begin with, and by the tenth century, if not before, they spoke Greek, so it is not clear that they constituted a separate ethnic group at all. The most that we can say based on the evidence is that they formed a distinct military corps in the empire, but one that was perhaps eventually manned completely by ordinary Romans. Possibly it was kept alive by military tradition, not the presence of a separate ethnic group. At any rate, it is not heard from again after the mid-tenth century.
zh: 马尔达伊特人（阿拉伯语称贾拉吉马，Jarajima）在阿拉伯征服后立即出现，是一个居住于基利家与叙利亚之间阿马诺斯山的尚武基督教群体。他们帮助皇帝对抗阿拉伯人，但基本自治，直到查士丁尼二世约687年与哈里发达成协议，将其中12,000人重新安置到帝国境内。
学者们争论过马尔达伊特人的族群起源，但史料没有明确指示；他们似乎是一个混合群体，实际上构成了自己的新认同。他们被分散到小亚细亚与希腊的海军军区，在九、十世纪有记载，充当桨手。911年远征包括5,087名西部马尔达伊特人，949年那次包括3,000名。
他们在基比拉奥特军区（阿塔莱亚）的队长似乎不受当地军事总督直接指挥，而由皇帝直接任命。
马尔达伊特人进入罗马军队服役后究竟构成何种群体，并不清楚。他们起初就是基督徒，到十世纪（若非更早）已说希腊语，因此他们是否构成一个独立族群并不清楚。依据证据我们最多能说，他们在帝国中形成了一支单独编制的部队，但或许最终完全由普通罗马人充任。或许军队沿用这个名称只是出于惯例，到了后来，已经没有独立的马尔达伊特族群。无论如何，十世纪中叶以后它不再见于记载。

en: In sum, foreign ethnic units complemented the Roman armies but only in marginal ways; they did not constitute its core. A force could include Rus’, Armenians, Slavs, and others and still be 90 percent Roman. This proportion holds for the use of Frankish mercenaries in the eleventh century: whenever numbers are cited, they are quite small, a few hundred here, a few hundred there.

The age of conquest would provide two significant exceptions to this pattern: a greater reliance on Armenians and the recruitment of the Varangian Guard, initially of six thousand men. We will discuss these groups in Chapter 7.
zh: 总之，外族部队只起辅助作用，罗马人仍是军队的主体。一支部队可以包括罗斯人、亚美尼亚人、斯拉夫人等，却仍有90%是罗马人。这一比例也适用于十一世纪法兰克雇佣兵的使用：凡有数字可查，人数都不多，通常每处不过几百人。
到了大举征服的时期，有了两项明显的例外：更倚重亚美尼亚人，以及征募最初达六千人的瓦良格卫队。我们将在第7章讨论这些群体。

en: Conclusions
zh: 结论

en: Was Romanía an empire in 930 ad? The short answer is that it was not. The vast majority of its population was Roman, and even beyond them it did not always exercise an “imperial” manner of rule over all its non-Roman subjects. A historian of ancient Rome has recently proposed that we think about Roman state power under three aspects: national power exercised by Romans over other Romans; imperial power by Romans over the non-Romans in their empire; and Roman power over people outside the empire. He finds that Byzantium after the seventh century does not really qualify as an empire.
My findings support this conclusion. A great deal of power had slid from the second (imperial) category into the first one (national). Romanía was the state of the Roman people and less of an empire.
zh: 公元930年的罗曼尼亚是一个帝国吗？简短的回答是：不是。其人口绝大多数是罗马人，而即便在他们之外，它也并不总是对其所有非罗马臣民行使“帝国式”的统治。一位古罗马史家最近提出，我们应从三个方面思考罗马国家权力：罗马人对其他罗马人行使的民族权力；罗马人对其帝国境内非罗马人行使的帝国权力；以及罗马人对帝国境外人群的权力。他认为七世纪以后的拜占庭并不真正够得上帝国。
我的发现支持这一结论。过去罗马人以征服者身份行使的许多权力，如今已成了在同一民族内部行使的权力。罗曼尼亚主要是罗马人的国家，具有帝国性质的部分较少。

en: To summarize our ethnic inventory of Romanía, the theme of Koloneia had a significant Armenian population, and there were Armenian minorities in Sebasteia and other neighboring themes. However, these populations had been living in the Roman empire for almost a millennium. It is likely that they were highly Romanized and Chalcedonian,

and they were not, as far as we know, treated differently by the state compared to provincial Romans. We do not know if auxiliary, ethnic Armenian units in the army were recruited primarily among them or in Armenia “proper.” Macedonia and Greece still had significant Slavic minorities, though these too had converted to Christianity and were Romanized to varying degrees. The imperial state had ceased to appoint or recognize local ethnic “chiefs” there and the territories in which Slavs had settled were under regular administration. The Sklabenoi of the theme of Strymon, in the hinterland of Thessalonike, seem by 904 to have been a regular part of the Roman army (if an unreliable one when the Arabs attacked the city in that year). We do not know what marked them as ethnically distinct at this point beyond the name attached to their units.
zh: 总结我们对罗曼尼亚的族群清单：科洛内亚军区有相当多的亚美尼亚居民，塞巴斯泰亚及其他邻近军区也有亚美尼亚少数群体。然而这些人口已在罗马帝国生活了近千年。他们很可能高度罗马化且属卡尔西顿派，

而且据我们所知，国家对待他们与对待行省罗马人并无不同。我们不知道军中由亚美尼亚族人组成的辅助部队主要从他们中征募，还是在亚美尼亚“本土”征募。马其顿与希腊仍有大量斯拉夫少数群体，尽管他们也已皈依基督教，并不同程度地罗马化。帝国国家已不再在那里任命或承认当地族群“首领”，斯拉夫人定居的地区处于常规行政管辖之下。斯特里蒙军区（在塞萨洛尼基腹地）的斯拉夫人（Sklabenoi），到904年似乎已成为罗马军队的常规组成部分（尽管那年阿拉伯人攻打该城时并不可靠）。除部队的名称以外，还不知道当时有什么表明他们是一个有别于其他人的族群。

en: By contrast, some people were subject to special arrangements. Jews could in theory and even practice be regarded as Roman citizens, but were also subject to discrimination, expulsions, and attempts to baptize them. The Ezerites and Milengoi in the Peloponnese also retained some sense of ethnic difference and a separate leadership, whatever their cultural profile was exactly. They formed a separate, quasi-autonomous enclave within Romanía. Apparently, so did the recently converted Hellenes of the Mani. The frontier in Thrace may, in 930, still have been home to Armenian and Syrian communities transplanted from the east almost two centuries earlier; or else they too may have been assimilated. Finally, the most “imperial” provinces were in Italy, where the local population was probably majority Lombard and Latin-speaking, though Calabria had a significant Greek-speaking population. Here the empire allowed its non-Romans to live according to their own norms and even laws, an important codification of difference. But it does not appear that they had lesser or fewer rights there in the eyes of the state as a result of this concession. No discrimination is attested in the sources on the grounds of ethnicity or religious rite.
zh: 相比之下，有些人受特殊安排约束。犹太人在理论上乃至实践中都可被视为罗马公民，却也遭受歧视、驱逐以及强制洗礼的企图。伯罗奔尼撒的埃泽里特斯人与米伦戈伊人同样保留了某种族群差异感与独立的领导层，不论其文化面貌究竟如何。他们在罗曼尼亚境内形成了一个独立的、准自治的飞地。马尼新近改宗、被称为“希腊人”的居民看来也是如此。色雷斯的边疆在930年可能仍是近两个世纪前从东部迁来的亚美尼亚与叙利亚社群的家园；抑或他们也已被同化。最后，最“帝国式”的行省在意大利，当地人口可能以伦巴第人、说拉丁语者为主，尽管卡拉布里亚有大量说希腊语的人口。在这里，帝国允许其非罗马人按自己的规范乃至法律生活，这是一项将群体之间的差别正式纳入法制的安排。但他们似乎没有因为这项安排而遭国家削减权利。史料中没有记载基于族群或宗教礼仪的歧视。

en: What does all this mean in practice? The vast majority of the subjects (or citizens) of Romanía were Romans. Even those subjects of Romanía who were described as ethnically different—primarily Slavs and Armenians at this time—were not subject to special legal regimes, especially if they were Orthodox, as most of them seem to have been. If they were treated differently it would have been in the regular course of social life, based on ethnic biases that seem to have permeated Roman society. But at the level of the state and its law of persons, the same institutions governed them as governed the Romans themselves. Members of these minorities could rise to the top, so long as they learned Greek and were Orthodox, but this brought them to the verge of becoming Romans themselves. Elite Romans who are described as having an ethnic origin occupied that liminal point. It is significant that the upper leadership of Romanía was almost entirely Greek-speaking and Orthodox: this means that ethnic minorities, even while subject in theory and likely in practice to the same laws and fiscal regimes as everyone else, faced ethnic or cultural impediments in their bids for positions of power. In this respect, Byzantium would have been perceived as “an empire of the Romans” to these minorities. On the other hand, it is clear that Jews (at select moments) and Paulicians (before their dispersal) could be targeted by the state for primarily religious reasons.
zh: 这一切在实践中意味着什么？罗曼尼亚的绝大多数臣民（或公民）是罗马人。即便是那些被描述为族群上不同的罗曼尼亚臣民——此时主要是斯拉夫人与亚美尼亚人——也不受特殊法律制度约束，尤其若他们是正教徒，而他们大多数似乎如此。若他们受到不同对待，那也会是在日常社会生活中，基于似乎渗透罗马社会的族群偏见。但在国家统治和关于个人地位的法律层面上，治理他们的制度与治理罗马人本身的制度相同。这些少数群体的成员可以升至顶层，只要他们学会希腊语且是正教徒，但做到这一点，他们就接近于成为罗马人了。那些被记作有外族出身的罗马精英，正处在这条界线上。意味深长的是，罗曼尼亚的上层领导几乎全说希腊语且为正教徒：这意味着即使少数族群原则上受同样的法律和财政制度约束，而且很可能实际上也是如此，他们在谋求权力职位时仍面临族群或文化障碍。在这方面，对这些少数群体而言，拜占庭会被视为“罗马人的帝国”。另一方面，很清楚，犹太人（在特定时刻）与保罗派（在其离散之前）可能主要因宗教原因被国家针对。

en: In short, most subjects of Byzantium in 930 did not have an “imperial” relationship to the state. They were ruled by institutions that could at times be oppressive, as institutions tend to be, but that otherwise operated within the undifferentiated framework of Romanía, a national state. For 930, at least, it is hard to justify the label “empire.” Its levels of ethnic diversity are strikingly low when compared to all other empires.
zh: 简言之，930年拜占庭的大多数臣民与国家之间并无“帝国式”关系。同不少制度一样，统治他们的制度也时有压迫，但罗曼尼亚作为一个民族国家，这些制度原则上并不因族群而异。至少对930年而言，很难证明“帝国”这个标签的正当性。与所有其他帝国相比，它的族群多样性低得出奇。

en: The Laz formed a client state in the fifth and sixth centuries, but it is not clear whether they lived in areas governed from Constantinople in the tenth (in the theme of Chaldia). Bryer, “Some Notes on the Laz,” hedges by saying that they were under Byzantine rule but de facto autonomous, yet there is no proof either way. It is perhaps significant that they are mentioned in sources relating to the empire of Trebizond, but not earlier. For the Laz today, see P. A. Andrews,

176–178; and Benninghaus, “Laz.” The Athinganoi were a heretical group in central Asia Minor, attested between the sixth and the ninth centuries, but not viewed as a separate ethnicity: Panagiotopoulos,

35 (citing previous bibliography). The emperor Michael II was believed to be associated with them somehow. Nothing indicates that the Tzakones (southeastern Peloponnese) were anything other than provincial Romans: Ilias Anagnostakis (pers. comm. and unpublished lectures). For the later meanings of the term, see Arhweiler, “Les termes Τσάκωνες”; Caratzas,
For ethnic monasteries, see Janin, “Les monastères nationaux,” and Kaldellis,

220n227; for monasteries in the sixth century named after provincial populations, possibly with ethnic or linguistic connotations, see Holl, “Das Fortleben,” 245 (e.g., “of the Lykaonians,” “Egyptians,” “Cretans,” but also “Antiochenes”). Arabs lived on Cyprus in the “condominium” phase, but they were presumably (and by definition) not under Roman jurisdiction.
